tracks.legalName: Automatic Expungement of Minor Cannabis Arrest Records
tracks.publicName: Checking whether your old cannabis arrest was already cleared automatically
tracks.mechanism: Minor cannabis offences committed before June 25, 2019, where one year or more has elapsed since the arrest and no charges were filed or charges were dismissed, vacated or resulted in acquittal, were expunged automatically by law enforcement on statutory deadlines that have all now passed. Separately, under § 5.2(a)(2.5) the citing agency and circuit clerks automatically expunge civil law violations of Cannabis Control Act § 4(a) or Drug Paraphernalia Control Act § 3.5(c) on or before January 1 and July 1 each year.
exclusions: Offences involving more than 30 grams, or carrying a penalty enhancement under Cannabis Control Act § 7, fall outside the 'minor cannabis offense' definition at § 5.2(a)(1)(G-5).
Records associated with an arrest, conviction or other disposition for a violent crime as defined in Rights of Crime Victims and Witnesses Act § 3(c).

State and the consequence of filing early before letting them proceed. Under Chastain a petitioner cannot use the liberal amendment rule to add records that were not yet eligible when the initial petition was filed, so filing now can permanently cost a record that ripens later. This is a delivery gate, not a generation blocker.

packetInstructions: Never say records are destroyed. In Indiana expungement means records are sealed or restricted under § 35-38-9-1(k). The Office of Judicial Administration states plainly that court records are not deleted or destroyed under I.C. 35-38-9.

Put only the last four digits of the Social Security number on the petition. The full number goes on the Confidential Information Form, filed as a confidential document, accompanied by the Notice of Exclusion of Confidential Information from Public Access. Do not persist the full number.
Disclose that the expungement case file is public until the order is granted.
The petition must not be filed without the written prosecutor consent § 35-38-9-5 requires. State this prominently in the filing instructions.
The court may reduce or waive the civil filing fee for an indigent petitioner under I.C. 35-38-9-8(d). Surface the waiver.
The prosecuting attorney must respond within 30 days of receipt and waives any objection by failing to respond, under I.C. 35-38-9-8(g).
scopeRestrictions: One petition per lifetime under § 35-38-9-9(i). Petitions filed in separate counties count as one only if they land inside a single 365-day window. Build the eligibility calendar and the 365-day window optimiser before the petition generator; in Indiana the scheduling decision is worth more than the document.

Put a hard gate in front of any conviction filing: where the participant has any conviction not yet eligible, surface Chastain v. State and the consequence of filing early before letting them proceed. Under Chastain a petitioner cannot use the liberal amendment rule to add records that were not yet eligible when the initial petition was filed, so filing now can permanently cost a record that ripens later. This is a delivery gate, not a generation blocker.

The prosecuting attorney's written consent is required to file at all on this track. Silence is not consent. Obtaining it is a participant action and a required-before-filing item, not a reason to withhold generation.
The grant is discretionary. Route to a legal-review gate before offering this track.

There is no Coalition for Court Access Section 5 insert to acquire. The published conviction inserts cover Sections 2, 3 and 4 only. The route uses a controlled statutory custom pleading with a verified local-form override, and yields to a published local form where one exists.

LegalEase does not obtain the prosecuting attorney's consent and does not negotiate for it. The packet carries the consent as an attachment or a clearly labelled placeholder, with instructions for requesting it. Where negotiation is needed this is an attorney-handoff point.

Bodily injury or serious bodily injury must be an element of the offence of conviction for the exclusion to apply, per Allen v. State, 159 N.E.3d 580 (Ind. 2020). The court nonetheless retains discretion and may consider the facts incident to the conviction.

The Coalition for Court Access base conviction petition and order bundle in the corpus is the 03/2020 revision and predates later amendments to the chapter. Retain it as a reference only; do not silently approve it as the Section 5 instrument.

tracks.legalName: Infraction Non-Disclosure under I.C. 34-28-5-15
tracks.publicName: Keeping an infraction off background checks
tracks.mechanism: The court must order the clerk and any case management system operator not to disclose infraction information to a non-criminal-justice organisation or individual where the person is not prosecuted, the charge is dismissed, the person is adjudged not to have committed the infraction, or an adjudication is later vacated. This does not apply where prosecution was deferred. Where the court failed to act, a petition branch applies with earliest filing dates. A deferral or satisfied judgment supports a verified petition no earlier than five years after satisfying the conditions.
exclusions: Cases where prosecution was deferred, for the automatic branch. Those use the five-year deferral branch instead.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Kansas District Court Conviction under K.S.A. 21-6614
tracks.publicName: Expunging a Kansas conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted in Kansas of a traffic infraction, cigarette or tobacco infraction, misdemeanour, class D or E felony, nongrid felony, nondrug grid severity level 6 through 10 felony, drug grid severity level 4 felony for crimes committed between July 1, 1993 and June 30, 2012, or drug grid severity level 5 felony for crimes committed on or after July 1, 2012, may petition the convicting court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records once the applicable period has elapsed since satisfying the sentence imposed or being discharged from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence. Longer periods apply under (c) and (d). At the hearing the court shall order expungement if it makes the four findings in (h). The clock runs from sentence satisfaction or discharge from supervision — not from arrest and not from conviction.
authority: State v. Anderson, 12 Kan. App. 2d 342, 744 P.2d 143 (1987)
exclusions: Rape, K.S.A. 21-5503 or former 21-3502.
Indecent liberties or aggravated indecent liberties with a child, K.S.A. 21-5506 or former 21-3503 or 21-3504.
Criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504(a)(3) or (a)(4) or former 21-3505(a)(2) or (a)(3).
Aggravated criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504 or former 21-3506.
Indecent solicitation or aggravated indecent solicitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5508 or former 21-3510 or 21-3511.
Sexual exploitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5510 or former 21-3516.
Internet trading or aggravated internet trading in child pornography, K.S.A. 21-5514.
Aggravated incest, K.S.A. 21-5604 or former 21-3603.
Endangering or aggravated endangering a child, K.S.A. 21-5601 or former 21-3608 or 21-3608a.
Abuse of a child, K.S.A. 21-5602 or former 21-3609.
Capital murder, K.S.A. 21-5401 or former 21-3439.
Murder in the first degree, K.S.A. 21-5402 or former 21-3401.
Murder in the second degree, K.S.A. 21-5403 or former 21-3402.
Voluntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5404 or former 21-3403.
Involuntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5405 or former 21-3404.
Sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3517, where the victim was under 18 at the time of the crime.
Aggravated sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3518.
A violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, including any diversion for such violation.

Any conviction for any offence in effect at any time prior to July 1, 2011 that is comparable to any offence in K.S.A. 21-6614(e). This reaches convictions under repealed pre-2011 offence definitions.
An attempt to commit any of the above.

Any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f), except through the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route.

waitingPeriods.condition: Traffic infraction, cigarette or tobacco infraction, misdemeanour, or class D or E felony
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the latest of satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.condition: Nongrid felony, or nondrug grid severity level 6 through 10, offence committed on or after July 1, 1993
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the same triggering events, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.condition: Drug grid severity level 4, offence committed on or after July 1, 1993 but before July 1, 2012
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the same triggering events, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.condition: Drug grid severity level 5, offence committed on or after July 1, 2012
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the same triggering events, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.condition: Class A, B or C felony; off-grid felony; nondrug grid severity levels 1 through 5; drug grid levels 1 through 3 for offences from July 1, 1993 to June 30, 2012, or levels 1 through 4 for offences on or after July 1, 2012

Vehicular homicide; driving while cancelled, suspended or revoked; perjury under K.S.A. 8-261a; fraudulent application under K.S.A. 8-142 Fifth; any felony in which a motor vehicle was used; failing to stop at an accident scene; no motor vehicle liability insurance under K.S.A. 40-3104; a violation of former K.S.A. 21-3405b
waitingPeriods.duration: 5 years, K.S.A. 21-6614(c)(1) through (c)(8)

waitingPeriods.condition: First violation of K.S.A. 8-1567, driving under the influence
Second or subsequent violation of K.S.A. 8-1567
waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years, K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(2). Subsection (d) applies to violations committed on or after July 1, 2006.

waitingPeriods.condition: Second or subsequent violation of K.S.A. 8-1567 committed on or after July 1, 2014 but before July 1, 2015
waitingPeriods.duration: 7 years. K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(3) disapplies the 10-year rule to that window, and the shorter period follows from the law in effect at the time of the offence under State v. Anderson.

tracks.venue: Statewide statute and statewide forms, executed county by county across 31 judicial districts. K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1) directs the petition to the convicting court. The Judicial Council instructions tell the participant to file with the clerk of the court in the county in which they were arrested. For the ordinary case these are the same county; where they differ, the statute governs and the participant confirms with the clerk.

destination.detail: All petitions for expungement are docketed in the original criminal action under K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(3). The Judicial Council instructions nonetheless require a Criminal Cover Sheet, whose own text says it initiates a criminal docket sheet. Provide the cover sheet and do not promise the participant a new case number.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name?

What sex, race and date of birth should the petition state?
In which Kansas county and which court was the case, and what is the case number?
Which law enforcement agency arrested you?
What offence were you convicted of, and under which Kansas statute?

packetInstructions: The packet carries a hearing-preparation document putting the four K.S.A. 21-6614(h) findings in plain language and prompting the participant to assemble their own account of the intervening years and their own supporting documents. Three of the four findings are unpleaded by the official petition. LegalEase does not write the participant's account of their own life and does not predict the outcome.

The packet must tell the participant exactly who completes what and in what order: which documents are for the clerk, which are brought to the hearing for the judge, and which goes to the KBI. A packet that hands someone five documents without saying so fails at the counter.
The required number of copies varies by county and there is no statewide answer. The packet instructs the participant to confirm the copy count with the clerk before filing.

Consumer copy must carry the disclosure carve-outs. After expungement the participant is treated as not having been arrested, convicted or diverted and may say so, but K.S.A. 21-6614(i)(2) lists twelve contexts where the arrest, conviction or diversion must still be disclosed, including law enforcement employment, a commercial driver's licence, bar admission, private detective and private patrol work, KDADS institutions, the Kansas lottery, racing and gaming, expanded lottery act positions, state and tribal gaming, securities registration, bail enforcement licensure, and insurance producer or public adjuster licensure for a fraudulent insurance act. Subsection (l) lists eighteen categories of requestor to whom the custodian may still disclose.

The packet must state the firearms-restoration effect. Under K.S.A. 21-6614(k)(2) a person whose expunged record had prohibited firearm possession is deemed to have had the right to keep and bear arms fully restored, and this applies to all orders of expungement including those issued before July 1, 2021; under (m)(2) the KBI reports to the FBI that the record be withdrawn from the national instant criminal background check system. LegalEase states the statutory effect and does not advise on federal firearms law.

The packet must say that the hearing is required and real: the prosecutor appears, any person with relevant information may testify, and the court may inquire into the participant's background with access to Department of Corrections and Prisoner Review Board records.
The docket fee of $176, plus any non-judicial personnel charge, accompanies the petition at filing.

That freezes every case in the record, not only the registrable offence. The sole exception is the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route; sex offender and violent offender registrants are barred with no exception.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Fulfilled Kansas Diversion Agreement under K.S.A. 21-6614
tracks.publicName: Expunging a Kansas diversion you completed
tracks.mechanism: A person who has fulfilled the terms of a diversion agreement may petition the district court to expunge the diversion agreement and related arrest records if three or more years have elapsed since the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled. The five-year lanes in (c) and the five-year first-violation DUI lane in (d)(1) reach diversions by their own terms; the 10-year lane in (d)(2) speaks only of satisfying a sentence or discharge from supervision and does not reach a diversion, which is why the Judicial Council chart shows not-applicable in the diversion column for the 7-year and 10-year DUI rows. The triggering event is fulfilment of the diversion terms, and nothing else.

packetInstructions: The packet carries a hearing-preparation document putting the four K.S.A. 21-6614(h) findings in plain language and prompting the participant to assemble their own account of the intervening years and their own supporting documents. Three of the four findings are unpleaded by the official petition. LegalEase does not write the participant's account of their own life and does not predict the outcome.

The packet must tell the participant exactly who completes what and in what order: which documents are for the clerk, which are brought to the hearing for the judge, and which goes to the KBI. A packet that hands someone five documents without saying so fails at the counter.
The required number of copies varies by county and there is no statewide answer. The packet instructs the participant to confirm the copy count with the clerk before filing.

Consumer copy must carry the disclosure carve-outs. After expungement the participant is treated as not having been arrested, convicted or diverted and may say so, but K.S.A. 21-6614(i)(2) lists twelve contexts where the arrest, conviction or diversion must still be disclosed, including law enforcement employment, a commercial driver's licence, bar admission, private detective and private patrol work, KDADS institutions, the Kansas lottery, racing and gaming, expanded lottery act positions, state and tribal gaming, securities registration, bail enforcement licensure, and insurance producer or public adjuster licensure for a fraudulent insurance act. Subsection (l) lists eighteen categories of requestor to whom the custodian may still disclose.

That freezes every case in the record, not only the registrable offence. The sole exception is the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route; sex offender and violent offender registrants are barred with no exception.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Prostitution Conviction or Diversion Where the Petitioner Was Acting Under Coercion, K.S.A. 21-6614(b)
tracks.publicName: Expunging a prostitution case where someone was coercing you
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of prostitution as defined in former K.S.A. 21-3512, or of a violation of K.S.A. 21-6419, or who entered into a diversion agreement in lieu of further criminal proceedings for such a violation, may petition the convicting court to expunge the conviction or diversion agreement and related arrest records if one or more years have elapsed since satisfying the sentence, fulfilling the diversion terms or discharge from supervision, and the person can prove they were acting under coercion caused by the act of another. Coercion is defined in the subsection as threats of harm or physical restraint against any person; a scheme, plan or pattern intended to cause a person to believe that failure to perform an act would result in bodily harm or physical restraint against any person; or the abuse or threatened abuse of the legal process.
exclusions: A case that is not a conviction of, or diversion for, prostitution under K.S.A. 21-6419 or former K.S.A. 21-3512.
A petitioner who cannot prove they were acting under coercion caused by the act of another. The coercion element is a proof burden at the hearing, not a formality.
A person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act, K.S.A. 21-6614(f).
The K.S.A. 21-6614(e) offence list, which continues to apply.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Immediate Expungement After Completing a Specialty Court Programme, K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3)
tracks.publicName: Expunging a conviction right after you finish a specialty court programme
tracks.mechanism: Notwithstanding the three-year rule in K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1), and except as provided in subsections (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f), a person who has completed the requirements of a specialty court programme established under K.S.A. 20-173 may petition the district court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records. There is no waiting period. The court may waive all or part of the docket fee imposed for filing a petition under this subsection. At the hearing the court need only find that no felony proceeding is presently pending or being instituted against the petitioner under (h)(1)(B); the two-year no-felony-conviction lookback in (h)(1)(A) does not apply to this lane. The other three findings continue to apply.
exclusions: Rape, K.S.A. 21-5503 or former 21-3502.
Indecent liberties or aggravated indecent liberties with a child, K.S.A. 21-5506 or former 21-3503 or 21-3504.
Criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504(a)(3) or (a)(4) or former 21-3505(a)(2) or (a)(3).
Aggravated criminal sodomy, K.S.A. 21-5504 or former 21-3506.
Indecent solicitation or aggravated indecent solicitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5508 or former 21-3510 or 21-3511.
Sexual exploitation of a child, K.S.A. 21-5510 or former 21-3516.
Internet trading or aggravated internet trading in child pornography, K.S.A. 21-5514.
Aggravated incest, K.S.A. 21-5604 or former 21-3603.
Endangering or aggravated endangering a child, K.S.A. 21-5601 or former 21-3608 or 21-3608a.
Abuse of a child, K.S.A. 21-5602 or former 21-3609.
Capital murder, K.S.A. 21-5401 or former 21-3439.
Murder in the first degree, K.S.A. 21-5402 or former 21-3401.
Murder in the second degree, K.S.A. 21-5403 or former 21-3402.
Voluntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5404 or former 21-3403.
Involuntary manslaughter, K.S.A. 21-5405 or former 21-3404.
Sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3517, where the victim was under 18 at the time of the crime.
Aggravated sexual battery, K.S.A. 21-5505 or former 21-3518.
A violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, including any diversion for such violation.

Any conviction for any offence in effect at any time prior to July 1, 2011 that is comparable to any offence in K.S.A. 21-6614(e). This reaches convictions under repealed pre-2011 offence definitions.
An attempt to commit any of the above.

Any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, K.S.A. 21-6614(f), except through the K.S.A. 22-4908 drug offender route.

Any offence that would sit in the five-year lane under K.S.A. 21-6614(c), the five-year or ten-year DUI lanes under (d), or the one-year prostitution lane under (b). The exceptions in (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f) all continue to apply, so the immediate route reaches only offences that would otherwise sit in the three-year lane.
A programme that was not a specialty court established under K.S.A. 20-173, including ordinary diversion and locally run programmes that do not qualify.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Kansas Arrest Record under K.S.A. 22-2410
tracks.publicName: Expunging an arrest that did not lead to a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Any person who has been arrested in Kansas may petition the district court to expunge the arrest record. There is no waiting period. On filing, the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and the official court file is separated from other court records and disclosed only to a judge, designated court staff, the prosecuting attorney, the arresting agency or others by court order. At the hearing the court shall order the arrest record and subsequent court proceedings expunged on finding that the arrest occurred because of mistaken identity, that a court found there was no probable cause for the arrest, that the petitioner was found not guilty, or that expungement would be in the best interests of justice and charges have been dismissed or no charges have been or are likely to be filed. This is the correct route for an arrest-only record: K.S.A. 21-6614 expunges a conviction or a diversion and related arrest records, so with neither there is nothing for it to attach to.
authority: State v. Yrigolla, 38 Kan. App. 2d 1029, 175 P.3d 276 (2008)
exclusions: A case in which the person was charged with and convicted of a crime, or entered into and completed a diversion agreement, which runs under K.S.A. 21-6614 instead. State v. Yrigolla holds that K.S.A. 22-2410 does not apply where a person was arrested and subsequently entered into and completed a diversion agreement to avoid a conviction.
An arrest on a violation of a city ordinance, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516a in the municipal court.

packetInstructions: The packet must tell the participant exactly who completes what and in what order: which documents are for the clerk, which are brought to the hearing for the judge, and which goes to the KBI. A packet that hands someone five documents without saying so fails at the counter.

The packet must state the fee position accurately. No surcharge or fee at all is imposed on a petitioner under (a)(1) who was arrested as a result of identity theft, or who has had charges dismissed because a court found no probable cause, or who was found not guilty, or whose charges have been dismissed. That reaches most arrest-only petitioners, and the $176 docket fee is charged only where none of those applies.

The packet must say that where the best-interests-of-justice ground is used, K.S.A. 22-2410(e) requires the court to determine whether the records should nonetheless remain available for eight enumerated purposes, and that on filing the official court file is separated from other court records.
participantQuestions: Ask whether the participant was convicted or completed a diversion in the case. If either happened, K.S.A. 21-6614 governs and this route does not apply, as the form's own Notes on Use and State v. Yrigolla record.

scopeRestrictions: The Kansas Judicial Council states its forms are for non-commercial use and may not be sold, republished or transferred for value without express permission. Every Kansas official-form route is source-gated on that licence until permission is confirmed.

The K.S.A. 22-2410(a)(2) mandatory expungement category is not a participant filing. Where a person was arrested as a result of mistaken identity or because another person used their identifying information and the charge is dismissed or not prosecuted, the prosecuting attorney or the judicial officer who ordered the dismissal or declined to prosecute provides notice to the court and petitions for expungement, and the court shall order it. LegalEase explains that route and does not file it or represent that it can.

tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of a violation of a city ordinance may petition the convicting municipal court to expunge the conviction and related arrest records once three or more years have elapsed since satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from probation, parole or a suspended sentence; a person who has fulfilled the terms of a diversion agreement based on a city ordinance violation may petition once three or more years have elapsed since those terms were fulfilled. Longer five-year and ten-year periods apply to the offences listed in (d) and to DUI-equivalent ordinance violations under (e), and a one-year period applies under (c) to a prostitution-equivalent ordinance violation where the petitioner can prove coercion. The court sets a hearing and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and shall order expungement on three findings: no felony conviction in the past two years with no such proceeding pending or being instituted, that the petitioner's circumstances and behaviour warrant expungement, and that expungement is consistent with the public welfare. There is no firearms finding, because a municipal ordinance conviction is not a felony.
exclusions: A conviction or diversion for a city ordinance violation that would also constitute a violation of K.S.A. 8-2,144, commercial driving under the influence, K.S.A. 12-4516(f).
A district court conviction or diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 21-6614.
An arrest with no municipal conviction and no municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516a.
A petitioner convicted of a felony within the past two years, or against whom such a proceeding is pending or being instituted, K.S.A. 12-4516(h)(1).

waitingPeriods.condition: Conviction of a city ordinance violation
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the latest of satisfying the sentence imposed or discharge from probation, parole or a suspended sentence, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1)

waitingPeriods.condition: Fulfilled diversion agreement based on a city ordinance violation
waitingPeriods.duration: 3 years from the date the terms of the diversion agreement were fulfilled, K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(2)

waitingPeriods.condition: An ordinance violation prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) and adopted before July 1, 2014
waitingPeriods.duration: none. K.S.A. 12-4516(b) states no elapsed period for this category.

waitingPeriods.condition: An ordinance violation that would also constitute prostitution under K.S.A. 21-6419 or former K.S.A. 21-3512, where the petitioner can prove coercion caused by the act of another
waitingPeriods.duration: 1 year from satisfying the sentence, fulfilling the diversion terms or discharge from supervision, K.S.A. 12-4516(c)

waitingPeriods.condition: An ordinance violation that would also constitute vehicular homicide, driving while cancelled, suspended or revoked, perjury under K.S.A. 8-261a, a fraudulent application under K.S.A. 8-142 Fifth, a felony in which a motor vehicle was used, failing to stop at an accident scene, no motor vehicle liability insurance under K.S.A. 40-3104, or a violation of former K.S.A. 21-3405b
An ordinance violation that would also constitute a first violation of K.S.A. 8-1567, driving under the influence
An ordinance violation that would also constitute a second or subsequent violation of K.S.A. 8-1567
waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years, K.S.A. 12-4516(e)(2). Subsection (e) applies to all violations committed on or after July 1, 2006, and the municipal statute has no equivalent of the K.S.A. 21-6614(d)(3) seven-year window.

tracks.venue: Statewide statute available in every Kansas municipal court, executed court by court. K.S.A. 12-4516(a)(1) directs a conviction petition to the convicting court, which is the municipal court of the city whose ordinance was violated, and (a)(2) directs a diversion petition to the court. Kansas has hundreds of municipal courts and no unified municipal forms regime, so the instrument is court-specific even though the mechanism is statewide.

packetInstructions: The packet must tell the participant to confirm with the municipal court clerk, before filing, whether that court publishes its own form, what it charges as costs, and how many copies it wants.

The municipal findings are three, not four. K.S.A. 12-4516(h) requires no felony conviction in the past two years with no such proceeding pending or being instituted, that the petitioner's circumstances and behaviour warrant expungement, and that expungement is consistent with the public welfare. There is no firearms-safety finding, because an ordinance conviction is not a felony conviction.

The disclosure carve-outs apply here too. K.S.A. 12-4516(i) tracks the district court effect: the petitioner is treated as not having been arrested, convicted or diverted, subject to an enumerated list of contexts in which the arrest, conviction or diversion must still be disclosed.
participantQuestions: Ask whether the ordinance violation would also have constituted a listed Kansas offence. The three-year, five-year and ten-year branches all turn on that, and the participant owns the answer.
scopeRestrictions: Kansas municipal courts publish their own expungement instruments and some govern by charter ordinance rather than by K.S.A. 12-4516 directly. Wichita Municipal Court proceeds under Charter Ordinance No. 224, §§ 12 and 13 and publishes a Motion and Order rather than a petition; Topeka Municipal Court cites K.S.A. 12-4516 and publishes its own petition and order forms. Where the municipal court publishes a current form or requires its own process, that local instrument governs and the statewide controlled pleading is not used.

LegalEase does not write the participant's showing that their circumstances and behaviour warrant expungement or that expungement is consistent with the public welfare. It prompts for the participant's own facts and formats them.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a City Ordinance Arrest Record under K.S.A. 12-4516a
tracks.publicName: Expunging an arrest on a city ordinance charge
tracks.mechanism: Any person who has been arrested on a violation of a city ordinance may petition the court to expunge the arrest record. When the petition is filed the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency, and the official court file is separated from other court records and disclosed only to a judge, designated court staff, the prosecuting attorney, the arresting agency or others by court order. A municipal court may prescribe a fee as costs, except that no fee may be charged to a person arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft. At the hearing the court shall order the arrest record and subsequent court proceedings expunged on finding mistaken identity; that a court found no probable cause for the arrest; that the petitioner was found not guilty; that the arrest was for a violation of an ordinance prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) adopted before July 1, 2014; or that expungement would be in the best interests of justice and charges have been dismissed or no charges have been or are likely to be filed.
exclusions: A municipal conviction or a fulfilled municipal diversion, which runs under K.S.A. 12-4516.
An arrest on a state law violation, which runs under K.S.A. 22-2410 in the district court.

waitingPeriods.condition: Any ground under K.S.A. 12-4516a(c)
waitingPeriods.duration: none. K.S.A. 12-4516a states no waiting period.

packetInstructions: The packet must state the identity-theft fee exemption: no fee may be charged to a person who was arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft under K.S.A. 21-6107 or its predecessor, even though the municipal court may otherwise prescribe a fee as costs.

The packet must say that on filing the petition the official court file is separated from other municipal court records and is disclosed only to a judge, designated court staff, the prosecuting attorney, the arresting agency or others by court order, and that after expungement the records may still be released to a criminal justice agency with a legitimate need.

Where the best-interests-of-justice ground is used, K.S.A. 12-4516a(e) requires the court to determine whether the records should nonetheless remain available for eight enumerated purposes. The packet must say so.
participantQuestions: The choice among the five statutory grounds is the participant's own. Mistaken identity, no probable cause, acquittal, the K.S.A. 12-16,134 prohibited-ordinance ground and best interests of justice are positions LegalEase records rather than decides.
scopeRestrictions: Kansas municipal courts publish their own expungement instruments and some govern by charter ordinance rather than by K.S.A. 12-4516 directly. Wichita Municipal Court proceeds under Charter Ordinance No. 224, §§ 12 and 13 and publishes a Motion and Order rather than a petition; Topeka Municipal Court cites K.S.A. 12-4516 and publishes its own petition and order forms. Where the municipal court publishes a current form or requires its own process, that local instrument governs and the statewide controlled pleading is not used.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Relief from Drug Offender Registration under K.S.A. 22-4908, Combined with Expungement under K.S.A. 21-6614
tracks.publicName: Getting off the drug offender registry so your record can be expunged
tracks.mechanism: K.S.A. 21-6614(f) bars expungement of any conviction or any part of the criminal record of a person required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act while registration is required, except as provided in K.S.A. 22-4908. Under that section a drug offender who has registered for at least five years after the date of parole, discharge or release, or five years from the date of conviction if not confined, may file a verified petition for relief from registration in the district court of the county of conviction. The Judicial Council has developed the petition form the statute requires. On relief the court orders removal from the registry and notifies the KBI within 14 days. Subsection (i) permits the offender to combine the petition for relief with a petition for expungement under K.S.A. 21-6614 where the offence requiring registration is otherwise eligible for expungement. Sex offenders and violent offenders are not authorised to seek relief.
exclusions: Sex offenders and violent offenders required to register. K.S.A. 22-4908 authorises relief for drug offenders only, and K.S.A. 21-6614(f) bars expungement for the rest with no exception.

An offender who has registered for less than five years after the date of parole, discharge or release, or less than five years from the date of conviction if not confined. Time in jail or prison, and time when the offender was not in substantial compliance with registration requirements, does not count.
An offender required to register under K.S.A. 22-4906(k) because of an out-of-state conviction who would still be required to register under the law of the state where the conviction occurred.
A further petition within three years of a denial, unless the court orders a shorter period.
A registrable offence that is not otherwise eligible for expungement, for the combined expungement unit.

Any period during which the offender is incarcerated, or does not substantially comply with registration requirements, does not count toward the five years.

units.label: Verified petition for relief from offender registration
units.description: The Kansas Judicial Council Petition for Relief from Offender Registration, 06/2022, filed in the district court of the county where the offender was convicted of the offence requiring registration, with the Order of Relief from Offender Registration Cover Sheet for the KBI. Items 1 through 9 are the participant's own identity, conviction, registration, compliance and treatment-provider facts, all of which LegalEase completes from their answers. Item 10, the showing that circumstances, behaviour and treatment history demonstrate sufficient rehabilitation and that registration is no longer necessary to promote public safety, is a participant-authored narrative that LegalEase prompts for and formats and never writes. The court sets the hearing and notifies the county or district attorney, who notifies victims; the court may order a risk assessment at the offender's expense; relief requires clear and convincing evidence.

units.label: Companion or combined expungement petition under K.S.A. 21-6614
units.description: The K.S.A. 21-6614 expungement packet for the registrable conviction, permitted by K.S.A. 22-4908(i) to be combined with the registration-relief petition where the offence is otherwise eligible for expungement. This unit is the conviction packet already modelled at ks-21-6614-conviction and is not duplicated here: the same Judicial Council petition, cover sheet, notice of hearing, order cover sheet and both proposed orders are used, on the same waiting-period and findings rules. It is a separate legal filing from the registration petition, with a different statute, a different notice set and a different standard of proof, which is why the route is composed rather than a single packet.

tracks.venue: Statewide statute and statewide Judicial Council form. K.S.A. 22-4908(d)(1) directs the verified petition to the district court in the county where the offender was convicted or adjudicated of the offence requiring registration; where the conviction was out of state, to the district court of any county where the offender is currently required to register. The companion expungement petition follows the K.S.A. 21-6614 venue rule.

rules.notice: When the petition is filed the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the county or district attorney in the county where the petition is filed. The county or district attorney notifies any living victim of the offence requiring registration whose address is known, or the family of a deceased victim if the family's address is known. The victim or the victim's family cannot be compelled to testify or to provide discovery to the offender.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name?
What was your full name at the time of the conviction for the drug offence requiring registration, if different from your name now?
What race, sex and year of birth should the petition state?
What drug offence or offences require you to register, and in which court were you convicted, and on what date?
Are you registered as a drug offender, rather than as a sex offender or violent offender? Only drug offenders may petition for relief.
What was your most recent date of parole, discharge or release, or were you never confined for the offence?
In which counties are you currently registered as a drug offender?
Have you substantially complied with all registration requirements for at least five years since that date?
Have you been arrested, convicted, adjudicated or entered into a diversion agreement for any crime during the period you have been required to register? If so, which?
What are the names of all treatment providers and agencies that have treated you for mental health, substance abuse and offence-related behaviour since the offence?

In your own words: how do your circumstances, behaviour and treatment history show that you are sufficiently rehabilitated, and that your registration is no longer necessary to promote public safety? This is item 10 of the official petition and it is yours to write; LegalEase formats it and does not write it or judge it.
If you were convicted in another state, are you still required to register under that state's law?
Has a petition for relief from registration been denied before, and if so on what date?
Do you also want to ask the court to expunge the conviction at the same time? K.S.A. 22-4908(i) lets you combine the two petitions where the offence is otherwise eligible.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Record of Arrest That Did Not Result in a Conviction (La. C.Cr.P. art. 976)
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 976(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest for a felony or misdemeanour that did not result in conviction where the person was not prosecuted and the time limitation has expired, the district attorney declined to prosecute every offence arising out of the arrest including because a pretrial diversion programme was completed, the proceedings were finally disposed of by dismissal, sustaining of a motion to quash or acquittal, or the person was judicially determined to be factually innocent and entitled to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8. Article 976(B) bars expungement of an arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, or a parish or municipal equivalent, where the person was placed in a pretrial diversion programme, until five years have elapsed since the date of arrest. Article 975 bars filing by a person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour. Relief is effectively mandatory: under Article 980 the court grants where no timely objection is filed and the mover is legally entitled.
exclusions: A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file the motion (Art. 975). This is a status bar that lifts when custody status changes, not a permanent eligibility bar.

An arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated under R.S. 14:98, or a parish or municipal ordinance equivalent, where the person was placed in a pretrial diversion programme, until five years have elapsed from the date of arrest (Art. 976(B)).
A conviction arising out of the arrest. Any charge on the arrest that resulted in a misdemeanour or felony conviction is outside this Article and belongs to Article 977 or Article 978.

waitingPeriods.condition: Arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, or a parish or municipal ordinance equivalent, where the person entered a pretrial diversion programme
waitingPeriods.duration: Five years from the date of arrest for that offence (Art. 976(B)). The Article 989 form carries a dedicated check-box for it.

waitingPeriods.condition: Every other Article 976 ground
waitingPeriods.duration: None. There is no waiting period; where prosecution was never instituted the ground is the expiry of the time limitation for prosecution itself.

tracks.venue: The court with trial jurisdiction over the offence in the parish of arrest, under Article 972.1: district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts.

destination.name: Clerk of court for the parish of arrest
destination.detail: File the Article 989 motion with the proposed Article 991 and Article 992 orders. The clerk collects the Article 983 fees at filing unless a returned Article 988 fee exemption is appended, and thereafter serves the district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting agency under Article 979.

components.conditionDescription: Generated wherever the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) exemption, which on this track is common.
Used only where the arrest carries more charges or counts than the Article 989 motion's own fields hold.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Bill of information or indictment for each charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Minute entry showing the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification letter verifying that the charges were refused
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the eligibility basis is that the district attorney declined to prosecute.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing for a letter verifying that the charges arising out of this arrest were refused. The packet includes a cover request naming exactly which certifications your chosen eligibility basis needs.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification letter verifying no participation in a pretrial diversion programme
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the eligibility or fee-exemption basis depends on the absence of pretrial diversion.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the district attorney's office in writing for a letter verifying that you did not participate in a pretrial diversion programme on this arrest. The Article 989 attachment checklist lists it, and the Article 988 fee exemption turns on the same fact.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order of factual innocence and entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that made the determination
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only where the eligibility ground is factual innocence under Art. 976(A)(4).
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that made the determination for a certified copy.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional. Pursue it only where the agencies will execute one; the track does not depend on it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: This is the agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form, and only they can execute it. tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge a Record of Arrest and Conviction of a Misdemeanor Offense (La. C.Cr.P. art. 977)
tracks.publicName: Clear a misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 977(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest and conviction of a misdemeanour on either of two grounds. Under (A)(1) the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 894(B), which is the separate Article 987 mechanism. Under (A)(2) more than five years have elapsed since the person completed any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, the person has not been convicted of any felony offence during that five-year period and has no felony charge pending; the motion must include a certification obtained from the district attorney verifying, to his knowledge, no felony convictions during the five-year period and no pending felony charges under a bill of information or indictment. Article 977(C) bars expungement where the misdemeanour conviction arose from circumstances involving or resulting from an arrest for a sex offence as defined in R.S. 15:541 — expressly preserving interim expungement under Article 985.1 — and where the conviction was for domestic abuse battery or for stalking under R.S. 14:40.2. Confirmed against the current official text, whose source notes run through Acts 2023, No. 342.
exclusions: A misdemeanour conviction that arose from circumstances involving, or is the result of, an arrest for a sex offence as defined in R.S. 15:541. Article 977(C)(1) expressly preserves interim expungement under Article 985.1, so the felony-arrest entry may still be cleared on the interim track even though the misdemeanour itself may not.
A misdemeanour conviction for domestic abuse battery (Art. 977(C)(2)).
A misdemeanour conviction for stalking under R.S. 14:40.2 (Art. 977(C)(3)).
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).
A first-offence possession of marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinol or chemical derivatives misdemeanour conviction is governed by Article 977(D) and its own Article 998 form, and is a separate track.

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 977(A)(1) — the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 894(B)
waitingPeriods.duration: None. The set-aside and dismissal is the qualifying event. Where it has not happened, the participant must first obtain it through the separate Article 987 track.

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 977(A)(2) — the five-year route
waitingPeriods.duration: More than five years from completion of any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, with no felony conviction during that five-year period and no felony charge pending. The clean-period test bars felony convictions only; it is not the felony track's any-criminal-offence test.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.

rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F) through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, but its grounds are non-conviction grounds, so it is rarely available on a conviction track. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

tracks.legalName: Motion for Expungement for Misdemeanor Conviction for a First Offense Possession of Marijuana (La. C.Cr.P. arts. 977(D), 998)
tracks.publicName: Clear a first-offense misdemeanor marijuana possession conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 977(D) provides that notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, a person may file a motion to expunge his record of arrest and conviction of a misdemeanour conviction for a first offence possession of marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinol or chemical derivatives thereof after ninety days from the date of conviction. It replaces both the Article 894(B) set-aside requirement and the five-year wait that Article 977(A) would otherwise impose. Article 986 makes Article 998 the form to be used, and Article 998 is a dedicated motion form for this category, separate from Article 989. Article 977(D) carries no sunset of its own and remains in the current official text with the Article 977 source notes running through Acts 2023, No. 342.
exclusions: A conviction that is not a first offence for possession of marijuana, tetrahydrocannabinol or chemical derivatives thereof. A second or later possession offence falls back to Article 977(A).
A felony marijuana conviction, which is Article 978 territory and subject to the Article 978(B)(3) controlled dangerous substance exclusions and their exceptions.
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).

rules.filing: File the Article 998 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of conviction, at any time after ninety days from the date of conviction. Article 986 makes Article 998 the form to be used for this category; the Article 989 form is not used here.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: The ordinary Article 983(A) cap of five hundred fifty dollars now applies. The three-hundred-dollar cap formerly in Article 983(M) — fifty dollars each to the Bureau, the sheriff and the district attorney and one hundred fifty to the clerk — was null, void and without effect and terminated on 1 August 2026 under Article 983(M)(5), and is now historical only. The clerk collects at filing and the fees are non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Expunge Record of Arrest and Conviction of a Felony Offense (La. C.Cr.P. art. 978)
tracks.publicName: Clear a felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: Article 978(A) lets a person move to expunge a record of arrest and conviction of a felony where the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 893(E); or where more than ten years have elapsed since the person completed any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, the person has not been convicted of any other criminal offence during that ten-year period and has no criminal charge pending, with a district attorney certification; or where the person is entitled to a first offender pardon for the offence, provided it is not a crime of violence or a sex offence. Article 978(B) bars expungement, and bars filing, where the person was convicted of the commission or attempted commission of a crime of violence under R.S. 14:2(B) unless Paragraph E applies; a sex offence or a criminal offence against a victim who is a minor under R.S. 15:541, with a narrow carnal-knowledge exception; a violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law, except five listed categories that may be expunged; or domestic abuse battery. Article 978(E) permits the court, after a contradictory hearing, to order expungement for aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities on the ten-year clean-period conditions. Read against the current official text, whose source notes now run through Acts 2024, No. 580.
exclusions: A crime of violence as defined by or enumerated in R.S. 14:2(B), unless the offence is one of the six named in Article 978(E) and the court grants relief after a contradictory hearing (Art. 978(B)(1)).

Notwithstanding any provision of Article 893, a sex offence or a criminal offence against a victim who is a minor as each is defined by R.S. 15:541, or any offence occurring before 18 June 1992 that would be so defined had it occurred on or after that date (Art. 978(B)(2)(a)).

A violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law (Art. 978(B)(3)), except any of the following, which may be expunged: possession of a controlled dangerous substance under R.S. 40:966(C), 967(C), 968(C), 969(C) or 970(C); possession with intent to distribute; a violation punishable by a term of imprisonment of not more than five years; a violation that may be expunged under Article 893(E); and a violation for which the person is entitled to a first offender pardon under La. Const. art. IV, § 5(E)(1).
A conviction for domestic abuse battery (Art. 978(B)(4)).
A first offender pardon route is unavailable where the offence is a crime of violence or a sex offence (Art. 978(A)(3)).
A person in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour may not file (Art. 975).

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 978(A)(1) — the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 893(E)
waitingPeriods.duration: None. The set-aside and dismissal is the qualifying event, and it is obtained on the separate Article 987 track.

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 978(A)(2) — the ten-year route
waitingPeriods.duration: More than ten years from completion of any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, with no conviction of ANY OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENCE during that ten-year period and no criminal charge pending. This is not the misdemeanour test with a larger number: the misdemeanour clean period bars felony convictions only, and this one bars any criminal offence.

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 978(A)(3) — the first offender pardon route
waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond entitlement to the pardon itself. Under R.S. 15:572 a first offender never previously convicted of a felony is automatically pardoned on completion of sentence without a Board of Pardons recommendation or gubernatorial action, but no pardon issues unless the court costs for the conviction are paid.

waitingPeriods.condition: Article 978(E) — the violent-offence lane for aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities
waitingPeriods.duration: More than ten years since completion of sentence, deferred adjudication, probation or parole, with no criminal conviction during that period and no pending charge, and only after a contradictory hearing at which the court may grant relief in its discretion.

tracks.venue: The district court with trial jurisdiction over the felony in the parish of conviction, under Article 972.1.

destination.name: Clerk of court for the parish of conviction
destination.detail: File the Article 989 motion with the proposed Article 991 and Article 992 orders. The clerk collects the Article 983 fees at filing and serves under Article 979.

components.conditionDescription: Generated only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) exemption. Louisiana State Police states that anyone ever convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony, is ineligible for it, so on this track it will almost never apply.
Used only where the arrest carries more charges or counts than the Article 989 motion's own fields hold.
Applies only where the felony conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification verifying no conviction of any other criminal offence during the ten-year period and no pending criminal charge. Article 978(A)(2) requires it and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request naming the exact certification and the ten-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it, and its absence is a filing requirement rather than a generation blocker.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(2) ten-year route and on the Article 978(E) lane.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution. Ask the clerk for a certified copy. Where no such order exists and Article 893 relief appears available, obtain it first on the separate Article 987 track and then return here.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Has a court already signed an order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution under Article 893(E)?" against Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the first offender pardon. Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Under R.S. 15:572 the pardon is automatic for a first offender on completion of sentence, but it does not issue while court costs for the conviction remain unpaid. If costs are outstanding, pay them and then request the pardon; this is the most common and most fixable obstacle on this route.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole, or the Department of Public Safety and Corrections
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(3) first offender pardon route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984. Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the order waiving the sex offender registration and notification requirements under R.S. 15:542(F). Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Article 978(B)(2)(b) makes such an order sufficient to meet the mover's burden of showing that a pre-15-August-2001 carnal knowledge conviction would today be misdemeanour carnal knowledge of a juvenile.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The court that issued the waiver
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to the narrow Article 978(B)(2)(b) carnal-knowledge exception.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency. The agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Optional, and not available on the Article 978(E) lane, where a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself.

participantActionRequired.description: Every finding, ruling, date, place and signature on the Article 991 Order — Article 991 Order — the ordering paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.

Every granting or denying paragraph, finding, date, place and signature on the Article 992 Order of Expungement — Article 992 Order of Expungement — the decretal paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.
Race and gender — Article 989 Motion, Part I Defendant Information.
The participant's signature and the date of signing — Article 989 Motion, unrepresented-mover signature block on the final page.
Every certification box and the district attorney's signature on the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption — Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, the certification section and signature block.
The whole of the Article 990 Affidavit of Response — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The clerk's service of the motion and of the order and judgment — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles. On the first offender pardon route the participant must also have paid the underlying court costs of the conviction, which is a precondition of the pardon rather than an expungement fee.

Article 983(F) through the Article 988 form in principle, but Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony. On a felony conviction track the exemption will almost never be available, and the packet says so rather than implying a waiver that will be refused.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
