releaseBlockers.question: The operative date of Laws 2026, chapter 70, section 5 must be confirmed before participant-facing instructions state it. The session law was retrieved on 2026-08-02: section 5 adds a new paragraph (f) to § 609A.015, subd. 5, under which the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension unseals a record and notifies the judicial branch if it later determines the record did not qualify for automatic relief, making that determination only from a record stored in its criminal history system, and the following paragraphs are renumbered (g) through (j). It does not alter the BCA's identification duty, the court-sealing window or victim notice. Chapter 70 states an effective date only for section 4 (1 January 2027), so section 5 falls to the default in Minn. Stat. § 645.02. Packet identity is unaffected because this route has no packet; the participant-facing warning that a Clean Slate grant may later be unsealed is an instruction change.

tracks.legalName: Written Demand for Destruction of Arrest Identification Data under Minn. Stat. § 299C.11, subd. 1(b)
tracks.publicName: Arrest record destruction request (no court case)
tracks.mechanism: On written demand, law enforcement and the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension must destroy arrest identification data — fingerprints and thumbprints, photographs, distinctive physical mark identification data, known aliases and street names, and all copies and duplicates — where the person has no felony or gross-misdemeanour conviction anywhere in the ten years immediately preceding determination of all pending criminal actions in their favour, and either all charges were dismissed before a determination of probable cause, or the prosecuting authority declined to file and a grand jury did not indict. Relief is mandatory on demand where the conditions are met. The Minnesota Judicial Branch publishes six sample demand letters.
exclusions: Section 299C.11, subd. 3(1) provides that the following are not a determination in favour of the arrested person: sealing under § 152.18, subd. 1, § 242.31 or chapter 609A; successful completion of a diversion programme; an order of discharge under § 609.165; and a pardon under chapter 638.
Any felony or gross-misdemeanour conviction, in or outside Minnesota, in the ten years immediately preceding determination of all pending criminal actions in the person's favour.

tracks.legalName: Prosecutor-Agreed Sealing under Minn. Stat. § 609A.025
tracks.publicName: Prosecutor-agreed record sealing
tracks.mechanism: Where the prosecutor agrees, the court shall seal without any petition unless it determines that the interests of the public and public safety in keeping the record public outweigh the disadvantages to the subject. The prosecutor's agreement is discretionary and, before agreeing, the prosecutor must make a good-faith effort to notify identifiable victims of the intended agreement and of the opportunity to object. One statewide mechanism with county-specific intake.
exclusions: Dispositions outside the § 609A.02, subd. 3 grounds population.
Pending charges, as under § 609A.02, subd. 3.

waitingPeriods.condition: The § 609A.02, subd. 3 waiting periods apply by reference
waitingPeriods.duration: As under subd. 3. For a person described in subd. 3(a)(2), diversion or stay of adjudication, the prosecutor's agreement may occur before or after the charges are dismissed.

units.label: Request to the prosecuting authority
units.description: The participant asks the prosecuting authority to agree to sealing. LegalEase identifies the correct prosecuting authority from the county and offence location and prepares the participant's factual summary. Which sub-branch applies depends on whether the county runs a published programme.

units.label: County portal application
units.description: Hennepin, Ramsey and Washington Counties run published online applications. These are third-party intake systems with their own field requirements, so LegalEase prepares the participant's factual summary and routes them to the county portal. It does not complete or submit a county portal application.

units.label: Written request to the county or city attorney
units.description: Where the county runs no published programme, the participant contacts the county or city attorney directly. LegalEase generates a participant-signed written request setting out the case, the disposition, the applicable § 609A.02, subd. 3 ground and the participant's own account. The Attorney General page is the statewide entry point for identifying the correct authority.

units.label: Court sealing on prosecutor agreement
units.description: Once the prosecutor agrees, the court shall seal without any participant petition, unless the public-interest balance goes the other way. There is nothing for the participant to file at this stage.

tracks.legalName: Inherent-Authority Petition to Seal Judicial Branch Records
tracks.publicName: Petition to seal court records only
tracks.mechanism: A judicially recognised inherent authority to seal judicial branch records, outside chapter 609A. Ambaye sets two grounds: where the petitioner's constitutional rights may be seriously infringed by retention of the records, or, where constitutional rights are not involved, whether expungement yields a benefit to the petitioner commensurate with the disadvantages to the public and the burden on the court. Under Schultz, absent constitutional infringement the judicial branch cannot order non-judicial records sealed, so relief reaches court records only.
authority: City of St. Paul v. Froysland, 246 N.W.2d 435 (Minn. 1976)
exclusions: Police, sheriff, prosecutor and BCA records, which remain public because relief reaches judicial branch records only.
The § 609A.02, subd. 4 registration bar, treated as a hard bar here as a matter of policy.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Arrest, Plea, Trial or Conviction (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.140)
tracks.publicName: Expunging a Missouri conviction
tracks.mechanism: Section 610.140 is Missouri's general expungement mechanism and the route most participants belong on. It was read in full from the Revisor's current text, effective 1 January 2025. Subsection 2(1) lets any person apply to any court in which the person was charged or found guilty for an order to expunge records of that arrest, plea, trial or conviction; subsection 1(1) defines "court" as any Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court, and subsection 1(2) defines "crime" as any offense, violation or infraction of Missouri state, county, municipal or administrative law. Subsection 2(2) requires the petitioner to list every crime sought to be expunged in the one petition and bars any crime excluded under subsection 3. Subsection 6 sets the six criteria the court may consider: at the time the petition is filed at least three years for a felony or one year for a misdemeanor, municipal violation or infraction has run from the date the petitioner completed any authorized disposition imposed under § 557.011; during that same period the petitioner has not been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony, excluding traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307; all obligations relating to the disposition are satisfied including fines and restitution; no charges are pending; the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to public safety; and the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it. A pleading that the petitioner meets criteria (5) and (6) creates a rebuttable presumption so long as (1) to (4) are satisfied, and the burden then shifts to the prosecuting or circuit attorney; a victim has an opportunity to be heard and the court may find that the continuing impact on the victim rebuts the presumption. The clerk gives notice to the prosecuting attorney, whose written objection is due within thirty days after receipt of service, and the court holds a hearing within sixty days after a written objection unless the parties agree otherwise. Subsection 8 makes relief mandatory once the criteria are met and requires an order of expungement or of dismissal within six months of filing. Subsection 12 dismisses a petition where the criteria are not met or false information was knowingly provided, and bars a further petition until a year has passed since the date of filing the previous one. Subsection 13 caps a lifetime at not more than three misdemeanor offenses or ordinance violations carrying an authorized term of imprisonment and not more than two felony offenses, with no limit on infractions, and subsection 2(3) lets crimes committed as part of the same course of criminal conduct go in a single petition and count only at the highest level. Subsection 14 requires the court to make a form available for pro se petitioners carrying the declaration under penalty of perjury, which is what CR360 is. Expungement here is closure under § 610.120, never destruction.
exclusions: Class A felonies (§ 610.140.3(1)).
Dangerous felonies as defined in § 556.061 (§ 610.140.3(2)).
Any offense requiring registration as a sex offender (§ 610.140.3(3)).
Any felony offense where death is an element of the offense (§ 610.140.3(4)).
Felony assault offenses, misdemeanor or felony domestic assault offenses, and felony kidnapping (§ 610.140.3(5)).
The specifically enumerated chapter 566 sex offenses and the listed offenses in other chapters (§ 610.140.3(6)).
Offenses eligible under § 610.130, so the first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense occupies its own lane and never routes here (§ 610.140.3(7)).
Intoxication-related traffic offenses and intoxication-related boating offenses, and operating an aircraft with an excessive blood alcohol content or while intoxicated (§ 610.140.3(8)).
Any ordinance violation substantially equivalent to an excluded offense (§ 610.140.3(9)).
Any offense of a motor vehicle law or ordinance committed by a person holding, or required to hold, a commercial driver's license (§ 610.140.3(10)).
Most unlawful use of weapons offenses under § 571.030, subject to the specific statutory exceptions (§ 610.140.3(11)).

A crime prosecuted outside Missouri or outside the jurisdiction of a Missouri court. § 610.140.2(2) reaches only crimes that occurred within Missouri and were prosecuted under the jurisdiction of a Missouri court.

A person whose § 610.140.13 lifetime caps are already exhausted, counting expungements granted under § 610.140 and, from the date § 610.141 becomes operative, automatic expungements granted under § 610.141 as well (§ 610.141.6 makes the caps combined).
Arrest-only records with no charge filed, which run on the separate § 610.140.7 route recorded as mo-610-140-arrest.

waitingPeriods.duration: Three years. Measured at the time the petition is filed, running back from the date the petitioner completed any authorized disposition imposed under § 557.011 — not from the arrest date and not from the conviction date.

waitingPeriods.condition: Misdemeanor, municipal violation or infraction (§ 610.140.6(1))
waitingPeriods.duration: One year, measured the same way: at the time the petition is filed, from the date the petitioner completed the authorized disposition.

waitingPeriods.condition: Clean period (§ 610.140.6(2))
waitingPeriods.duration: The same three-year or one-year period, and the direction matters. The period runs backward from the filing of the petition, not forward from completion of the sentence. During it the petitioner must not have been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony, excluding traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307.

tracks.venue: Any Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty (§ 610.140.1(1) and 2(1)). Rule 155.01 commences the action by filing a petition in the circuit court of the county in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty. Where the participant's crimes were charged in more than one county the petition cannot reach them all: § 610.140.2(2) requires every crime in one petition but subsection 2(1) fixes venue by court of charge or finding of guilt, so a multi-county record is a self-help stop rather than a routing choice LegalEase makes.

destination.name: Clerk of the Missouri court where the petitioner was charged or found guilty
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the municipal, associate circuit or circuit court where the crimes were charged or the finding of guilt entered. Missouri has forty-six judicial circuits covering 114 counties and the City of St. Louis, plus municipal divisions. The clerk assigns the case number, gives notice of the filing to the prosecuting attorney under § 610.140.6, and distributes the order under § 610.140.8. Local filing practice, copy counts and fees are confirmed with that clerk and are not optional.

components.conditionDescription: Generated where the participant's court expects the petitioner to tender a proposed judgment. Missouri circuits differ: some clerks and judges prepare the judgment themselves under Rule 155.05, others expect it with the petition.
Generated where the agency defendant list or the offense table exceeds the space on the form. CR360 twice directs the petitioner to attach additional sheets as necessary.
Generated only where the participant answers that they cannot pay the filing fee and court costs.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Case.net printout for each case. Search Case.net by your name, and by every name variant and spelling you have used, for every county you have lived in or been charged in. Print the case summary and the docket for each matter. Case.net does not show every municipal division, so it is a starting point rather than a complete record.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition." against Case.net printout for each case, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case. Ask the clerk of each court for a certified copy of the docket sheet and the judgment or final disposition. A per-page or per-document fee usually applies. This is the document that proves the case number, the court, the offense description and the disposition date.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where each case was charged or the finding of guilt entered

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date." against Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Probation or parole discharge document. Ask your former probation or parole officer, or the Division of Probation and Parole, for the discharge document showing the date supervision ended. The waiting period runs from the day you completed the authorized disposition, and for a supervised case that is usually this date.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Corrections, Division of Probation and Parole, or the supervising court
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the disposition included probation or parole.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date." against Probation or parole discharge document, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the disposition included probation or parole.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Receipts or a clerk's payment history for fines, costs and restitution. Ask the clerk for the payment history on each case, showing a zero balance. Paragraph 3 of CR360 has you swear that all obligations relating to the disposition are satisfied, including fines and restitution, and an unpaid balance is a common and avoidable reason a petition is dismissed.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?" against Receipts or a clerk's payment history for fines, costs and restitution, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record. Request your own criminal record through MACHS. A name-based search shows open records; a fingerprint-based search is the only way to see records that are already closed, including anything already closed by law under § 610.105. Confirm the current fees with the Patrol before ordering, and note that fingerprint capture carries a separate vendor service fee.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction." against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Missouri Department of Revenue driver record. Order your Missouri driver record from the Department of Revenue. It shows administrative actions the court file will not, and it is the record that tells you whether a commercial driver licence issue is in play — which is an outright exclusion under § 610.140.3(10).
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where any case involves a traffic offense, an alcohol-related matter, or a commercial driver licence question.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?" against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where any case involves a traffic offense, an alcohol-related matter, or a commercial driver licence question.

The statewide revision is used, never the Jackson County variant in the corpus. The order granting leave to proceed as a poor person is on page two of the form and is the court's to sign.
rules.notice: The clerk of the court gives notice of the filing to the office of the prosecuting attorney that prosecuted the crimes listed (§ 610.140.6). The petitioner does not serve the prosecutor. If no objection is filed within thirty days after receipt of service the court may still set a hearing and must give reasonable notice to each entity named in the petition. A victim of a listed crime has an opportunity to be heard at any hearing.
rules.service: None performed by the participant. Notice is the clerk's function under § 610.140.6, and CR360 carries no certificate of service for the petitioner to complete. Rule 155.03 governs service in an expungement action.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs CR360 beneath the declaration required by § 610.140.14: I declare under penalty of perjury that the statements made herein are true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information, and belief. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank. The GN10 affidavit is separately sworn by the participant.
rules.notarization: none. CR360 uses a declaration under penalty of perjury rather than a notarial acknowledgment. This is the opposite of CR145 on the § 610.122 track, which must be subscribed and sworn before a notary, judge or clerk, and the two must not be conflated in participant copy.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name a Missouri case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.

List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition.
Were all of the cases you listed charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in the same Missouri county? If they were in different counties, one petition cannot reach them all.
For each case, was the offense a felony, a misdemeanor, a municipal or ordinance violation, or an infraction?

For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date.
Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?
Since the date you finished each case, have you been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any criminal charges pending right now, anywhere?

Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction.

Were any of the cases you listed part of the same course of criminal conduct, or charged as counts in the same indictment or information? If so they can go in one petition and count only once, at the highest offense level.

Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Work from your own paperwork: the circuit court division, any municipal division, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county, the Missouri Department of Revenue, and anyone else. Add every agency whose name appears on any document you have.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Case.net printouts, your court paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?

The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Missouri Supreme Court Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and the number is not published through Case.net. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

Is any case on your list a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for unlawful use or possession of drug paraphernalia? From 1 January 2027 at the latest, Missouri will expunge some of those automatically and free of charge, and an automatic expungement uses up the same lifetime slots as this petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case.net printout for each case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Search Case.net by your name, and by every name variant and spelling you have used, for every county you have lived in or been charged in. Print the case summary and the docket for each matter. Case.net does not show every municipal division, so it is a starting point rather than a complete record.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where each case was charged or the finding of guilt entered
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of each court for a certified copy of the docket sheet and the judgment or final disposition. A per-page or per-document fee usually applies. This is the document that proves the case number, the court, the offense description and the disposition date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Probation or parole discharge document
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Corrections, Division of Probation and Parole, or the supervising court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the disposition included probation or parole.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask your former probation or parole officer, or the Division of Probation and Parole, for the discharge document showing the date supervision ended. The waiting period runs from the day you completed the authorized disposition, and for a supervised case that is usually this date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Receipts or a clerk's payment history for fines, costs and restitution
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the payment history on each case, showing a zero balance. Paragraph 3 of CR360 has you swear that all obligations relating to the disposition are satisfied, including fines and restitution, and an unpaid balance is a common and avoidable reason a petition is dismissed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal record through MACHS. A name-based search shows open records; a fingerprint-based search is the only way to see records that are already closed, including anything already closed by law under § 610.105. Confirm the current fees with the Patrol before ordering, and note that fingerprint capture carries a separate vendor service fee.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri Department of Revenue driver record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where any case involves a traffic offense, an alcohol-related matter, or a commercial driver licence question.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Missouri driver record from the Department of Revenue. It shows administrative actions the court file will not, and it is the record that tells you whether a commercial driver licence issue is in play — which is an outright exclusion under § 610.140.3(10).

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 5 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to the public safety of the state
manualCompletionItems.why: It is a conclusion about the participant, sworn under penalty of perjury, and § 610.140.6(5) makes it one of the two criteria that create the rebuttable presumption. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own facts and never asserts the conclusion. The review lists it first among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 7 — that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it
manualCompletionItems.why: The same reason. § 610.140.6(6) makes it the second presumption criterion, and it is a legal conclusion about the public interest rather than a fact about the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection and the court and case number of any prior expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether prior expungements have exhausted the § 610.140.13 caps is a legal judgment the review lists among the questions requiring individualized legal judgment. LegalEase asks for the participant's history, records their answer, and does not decide whether the caps remain available.

manualCompletionItems.item: Final verification of the defendant agency list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 1, defendant selections and the Other lines
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.140.8 and the CR360 text both say the court's order of expungement shall not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant. A named agency closes its record; an unnamed agency keeps its copy, and the participant usually discovers that only when a later background check comes back. LegalEase builds the best list it can from the participant's own records because doing it badly is the most common way Missouri relief half-works, but the list is an assertion under oath about where records exist and the participant confirms it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number in the caption
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360, FI-05, CR370 and GN10 captions
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk assigns it when the petition is filed.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and the date
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, below the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own sworn statement. LegalEase never signs it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR370, Judgment and Order of Expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: The judgment is the court's. LegalEase supplies the caption and the recital of what was requested, nothing more.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time, division and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets a hearing only after the objection window, and supplies the details. The packet is generated long before they exist.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any statement that a particular offense is or is not on the § 610.140.3 exclusion list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: Several exclusions turn on classification rather than on the offense name — whether a felony is a dangerous felony under § 556.061, whether an ordinance violation is substantially equivalent to an excluded offense, whether a § 571.030 weapons offense falls in a statutory exception. The review makes never auto-screening the eleven categories from self-report an express limitation, and it is a self-help boundary.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraphs 5 and 7, paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection, the participant's signature and date, the case number, the hearing details, and the judge's findings and signature on CR370 are all left blank by design.
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

selfHelpBoundaries: Any case that may fall in one of the eleven § 610.140.3 exclusion categories, including any felony assault, domestic assault, kidnapping, sex, weapons, child or death-related offense.
Any sex-offender registration issue, current or historic.
Any intoxication-related traffic, boating or aircraft offense, which is excluded here and belongs on the § 610.130 route if anywhere.
Any commercial driver licence or commercial motor vehicle involvement.
Any § 571.030 unlawful use of weapons offense, including where a statutory exception may apply.
Any question whether the § 610.140.13 lifetime caps remain available, or whether an automatic § 610.141 expungement has already consumed one.
Any question whether separate cases were part of the same course of criminal conduct.
Cases charged in more than one Missouri county, which one petition cannot reach.
Any uncertainty about the exact date the authorized disposition was completed.
The prosecuting attorney files a written objection, or a victim appears or asks to be heard.
The court sets a contested hearing.
A previous petition was dismissed, which bars refiling until a year has passed since the date that petition was filed.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant asks about firearm rights, professional licensing, foster care or adoption, banking, insurance, gaming or federal employment.

The eleven § 610.140.3 exclusion categories are never auto-screened from participant self-report. Several turn on classification rather than on the offense name, and a wrong answer costs the participant a year's refiling bar.

A drink- or drug-driving matter must never be routed through § 610.140. § 610.140.3(7) and (8) exclude offenses eligible under § 610.130 and intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses generally, so the two routes do not overlap.

Self-help ends if the prosecuting attorney files a written objection within the thirty-day window, if a victim asks to be heard, or if the court sets a contested hearing. The initial packet is not retracted; the participant needs a lawyer for what happens next.

packetInstructions: Missouri expungement under § 610.140 is closure under § 610.120, not destruction. The record is closed to public access and specified entities keep access. Never say erased or destroyed on this track. Destruction language is accurate only under § 610.124 on the § 610.122 arrest track.

The order does not affect any entity not named as a defendant (§ 610.140.8). The packet builds the best agency list it can from the participant's own records, includes the current CR360 agency categories and free-text lines for others, and prints the warning that an omitted agency keeps its copy.

The refiling bar appears prominently above the signature block. Under § 610.140.12, if the court finds the petitioner has not met the criteria for any listed crime, or knowingly provided false information, it dismisses the petition and no further petition may be filed until a year has passed since the date the previous petition was filed — measured from the filing date, not from the dismissal.

Disclosure survives expungement in six situations and the participant must be told: an application for a licence, certificate or permit issued by Missouri to practise the participant's profession (§ 610.140.10(1)); any licence issued under chapter 313 or permit issued under chapter 571 (§ 610.140.10(2)); paid or unpaid employment with an entity licensed under chapter 313, any state-operated lottery, or any emergency services provider including any law enforcement agency (§ 610.140.10(3)); employment with a federally insured bank, savings institution or credit union or an affiliate, for 12 U.S.C. §§ 1829 and 1785 compliance (§ 610.140.10(4)); employment with an entity engaged in the business of insurance or any insurer, for 18 U.S.C. §§ 1033 and 1034 compliance (§ 610.140.10(5)); employment with any employer required by federal or state law to exclude applicants with certain criminal convictions (§ 610.140.10(6)). Outside those, § 610.140.11 lets the participant answer no to an employer's inquiry where no public record remains.

An expunged crime may still be considered a prior offense in determining a sentence for any later offense (§ 610.140.9), and the participant must disclose it to any court when asked or on being charged with a subsequent crime. Expungement is not erasure for sentencing purposes.
Do not quote the repealed $250 surcharge. § 488.650 was repealed effective 28 August 2023. Filing fees are ordinary circuit court fees, are county-variable, and are confirmed with the clerk.

FI-05 with case type code X5 is a required component of every § 610.140 packet, and the code is read from the Case Types List's circuit column rather than inferred from the track name. The review is right that a packet without the cover sheet and the right code gets bounced at the counter.

Where the participant reports a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for drug paraphernalia, the packet must explain the § 610.141 timing trade-off before they file: automatic expungement is free, is due no later than 1 January 2027, and consumes the same lifetime slots, so petitioning now may spend a slot on relief that was about to arrive at no cost. The packet must not promise that automatic relief will reach any particular record.

The certified docket and judgment, the payment history, the probation or parole discharge document and the Highway Patrol criminal record are obtained and attached by the participant before filing. None of them delays generation of the packet.
participantQuestions: The full Social Security number is required on FI-05 under Operating Rule 4.07 where the party is a person and it is reasonably available. It is asked once, placed only on the confidential sheet, and is not repeated on CR360, which does not request it.

The clean period runs backward from the filing of the petition, not forward from completion of the sentence, and the direction changes who is eligible. The intake asks the completion date and the conviction history separately for this reason.
scopeRestrictions: The lifetime caps are three misdemeanor offenses or imprisonable ordinance violations and two felony offenses, with no limit on infractions (§ 610.140.13). From the date § 610.141 becomes operative those caps are shared with automatic drug expungements under § 610.141.6, which counts expungements under both sections combined. The track is offered within those caps and never asserts that they remain available.

Offered only where every crime the participant wants expunged was charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in one Missouri county. A multi-county record cannot be reached by one petition and is routed to counsel.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: The lifetime caps are three misdemeanor offenses or imprisonable ordinance violations and two felony offenses, with no limit on infractions (§ 610.140.13). From the date § 610.141 becomes operative those caps are shared with automatic drug expungements under § 610.141.6, which counts expungements under both sections combined. The track is offered within those caps and never asserts that they remain available.

Open question blocks release (packet_components): The printed revision and current publication status of CR370, the Judgment and Order of Expungement under § 610.140. The form exists and is published by the Office of the State Courts Administrator — Missouri circuit clerks list it by number and title in their own form indexes — but courts.mo.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval from this environment, so no binary could be acquired and no revision stamp confirmed. Neither the repository corpus nor Master Library Edition 1.1 holds it; the repository's own artifact registry carries a CR370 row recorded as missing. The packet identity does not depend on it, but the proposed-order component cannot be field-mapped or rendered until the original is obtained.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): Whether any Missouri circuit requires a locally drafted proposed judgment, or prepares the judgment itself under Rule 155.05, rather than accepting CR370 tendered with the petition. Missouri practice differs by circuit and the review left it unresolved whether any circuit rejects the statewide form in favour of a local one. The track carries localFormOverride and the proposed order is a conditional component for this reason.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): The current standard circuit filing fee and cost schedule for a § 610.140 expungement case. County-variable and not published centrally. Rule 155.02 governs filing fees and costs but does not fix an amount. No fee figure is published on this track; the participant confirms with the clerk before filing.

Open question blocks release (correct_form): Whether the current SJRC (10-24) CR360 remains the published revision as of the current date. The corpus copy is SJRC (10-24) and Master Library Edition 1.1 retains it as a packet-form candidate; the Missouri Courts expungement forms index reports its expungement form set as updated 1 January 2025, which is consistent with a form stamped 10-24 being published effective 1 January 2025 alongside the S.B. 754 amendments. Byte-level confirmation against the publisher could not be made because courts.mo.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval.

Open question blocks release (participant_instructions): CR360 does not recite the § 610.140.13 lifetime caps anywhere on its face. The 2024 S.B. 754 limits — not more than three misdemeanor offenses or imprisonable ordinance violations, not more than two felony offenses, no limit on infractions — govern eligibility but appear only in paragraph 6's open-ended prior-expungement disclosure. The packet must carry the caps as an instruction; a participant working from the form alone would not learn of them.

Open question blocks release (venue): How a participant with cases charged in more than one Missouri county obtains complete relief. § 610.140.2(2) requires every crime sought to be expunged to be listed in the one petition, while § 610.140.2(1) fixes venue by the court where the person was charged or found guilty; the two cannot both be satisfied across counties. The review records multi-county records as a referral trigger and the track treats it as a hard self-help stop rather than resolving it.
One or more official sources have no recorded SHA-256, so staleness cannot be detected.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Records Related to an Arrest for an Eligible Crime (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.140.7)
tracks.publicName: An arrest that never became a charge
tracks.mechanism: Section 610.140.7 is a distinct petition inside the general expungement section and it was read verbatim from the Revisor's current text. It provides that a petition to expunge records related to an arrest for an eligible crime may be made in accordance with the provisions of the section to a court of competent jurisdiction in the county where the petitioner was arrested no earlier than eighteen months from the date of arrest, provided that during that time the petitioner has not been charged and has not been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense. Two things follow and both were disputed in the retained review. The waiting period is eighteen months, not three years: the internal LegalEase reference was correct and the secondary source quoting three years was quoting a superseded version. And venue is the county of arrest, which differs from the court-of-charge rule that governs the conviction route. The eleven exclusion categories in § 610.140.3 apply unchanged, because the arrest must be for an eligible crime. Relief is mandatory under § 610.140.8 once the criteria are met, the clerk's notice, the thirty-day objection window, the sixty-day hearing rule and the six-month decision deadline all apply, and the effect is closure under § 610.120. This route is not § 610.122: that is a narrower false-information or qualifying-moving-violation mechanism with a different court, a different division, a fingerprint card, notarization and destruction rather than closure.
exclusions: Class A felonies (§ 610.140.3(1)).
Dangerous felonies as defined in § 556.061 (§ 610.140.3(2)).
Any offense requiring registration as a sex offender (§ 610.140.3(3)).
Any felony offense where death is an element of the offense (§ 610.140.3(4)).
Felony assault offenses, misdemeanor or felony domestic assault offenses, and felony kidnapping (§ 610.140.3(5)).
The specifically enumerated chapter 566 sex offenses and the listed offenses in other chapters (§ 610.140.3(6)).
Offenses eligible under § 610.130, so the first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense occupies its own lane and never routes here (§ 610.140.3(7)).
Intoxication-related traffic offenses and intoxication-related boating offenses, and operating an aircraft with an excessive blood alcohol content or while intoxicated (§ 610.140.3(8)).
Any ordinance violation substantially equivalent to an excluded offense (§ 610.140.3(9)).
Any offense of a motor vehicle law or ordinance committed by a person holding, or required to hold, a commercial driver's license (§ 610.140.3(10)).
Most unlawful use of weapons offenses under § 571.030, subject to the specific statutory exceptions (§ 610.140.3(11)).
Any arrest where the petitioner was charged during the eighteen months following the arrest. § 610.140.7 requires that the petitioner has not been charged during that time.
Any arrest where the petitioner was found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense during the eighteen months following the arrest.
An arrest that became a charge and then a conviction, plea or finding of guilt, which runs on mo-610-140-conviction instead.

An arrest based on false information, or an arrest for a chapter 303 misdemeanor or qualifying moving violation that was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, where the participant seeks destruction rather than closure. Those belong on mo-610-122-arrest-expungement, which is a different statute, court and division and a materially stronger remedy.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name you may have been arrested under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.
On what date were you arrested? The eighteen-month waiting period runs from this date.
In which Missouri county were you arrested? If the arrest happened inside a municipality, name the municipality too. This petition is filed in the county of arrest.
Which agency arrested you?
What offense were you arrested for, as it appears on the arrest paperwork or on your Highway Patrol record?

Were you ever formally charged in court for this arrest — an information, an indictment, a complaint, a summons or a ticket that opened a court case? If a case was opened, this is not the right route.
Since the date of that arrest, have you been charged with any other criminal offense?
Since the date of that arrest, have you been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense?

Was the offense you were arrested for a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense requiring sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an equivalent ordinance violation, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Was your arrest based on false information, or was it for a chapter 303 misdemeanor or a moving violation that was later dismissed, nolle prossed or ended in a not-guilty finding? If so there is a stronger Missouri route under § 610.122 that destroys the record rather than closing it, and you should look at that first.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this arrest? Start with the arresting agency, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for the county, the court, and the Missouri Department of Revenue.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Highway Patrol record and your arrest paperwork and confirmed this list is complete?
Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number and the offense level.
The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

selfHelpBoundaries: The participant is unsure whether charges were ever filed on the arrest.
The offense of arrest may fall in any of the eleven § 610.140.3 exclusion categories.
The arrest may qualify under § 610.122 for destruction rather than closure, which is materially better relief and a different packet.
The participant was charged, or found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony, at any point in the eighteen months after the arrest.
The arrest date cannot be established from the Highway Patrol record or from agency paperwork.
The arrest occurred in one county and any charge was or would have been filed in another.
The prosecuting attorney objects, or the court sets a contested hearing.
There are arrests in more than one county.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant asks about firearm rights, professional licensing, banking, insurance or federal employment.

Where the participant may qualify under § 610.122 the packet says so and stops, because destruction under § 610.124 is materially better relief than closure and choosing between them is a legal judgment.
Self-help ends on a written prosecutorial objection or a contested hearing. The packet is not retracted.

packetInstructions: The waiting period is eighteen months from the date of arrest, read verbatim from § 610.140.7. The three-year figure appearing in secondary sources is superseded and is never published on this track or used in screening.
Venue is the county of arrest, not the court of charge. This is the one venue rule in Missouri that differs from the general expungement route and the packet states it plainly.
Relief here is closure under § 610.120. Only the § 610.122 route produces destruction under § 610.124. The packet must not describe an arrest expunged under § 610.140.7 as destroyed.
The fingerprint-based Highway Patrol record and the Case.net search confirming no case was opened are obtained by the participant before filing. Neither delays generation.

releaseBlockers.question: How an arrest-only § 610.140.7 petition should be presented on CR360, whose printed body text is written for convictions. The form says all of the convictions listed below occurred and were prosecuted within the state of Missouri and that the petition is filed in the county where the conviction was charged or the petitioner found guilty, both of which are wrong for an arrest with no charge filed in the arrest county. tracks.legalName: Closure of Official Records on Nolle Prosequi, Dismissal, Acquittal or Suspended Imposition of Sentence (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.105)
tracks.publicName: Cases that already closed by law
tracks.mechanism: Section 610.105 was read in full from the Revisor's current text, effective 28 August 2006, and it is short. Subsection 1 provides that where the imposition of sentence is suspended in the court in which the case originated, or where a case is nolle prossed, dismissed, or the accused is found not guilty, official records pertaining to the case shall thereafter be closed records when the case is finally terminated, except as provided in subsection 2 and in § 610.120, save that the judgment or order of the court remains a public record. Where a not-guilty finding rests on mental disease or defect excluding responsibility under § 552.030, the records close upon that finding and access is limited to law enforcement, child-care agencies, facilities defined in § 198.006 and in-home services providers defined in § 192.2400. Subsection 2 supplies the section's only exception: where the charge is a chapter 566 offense or one of the enumerated offenses in §§ 568.045, 568.050, 568.060, 568.065, 568.175 or 573.200 and 573.205, and the imposition of sentence was suspended, the records shall be made available to the victim for use in the victim's own judicial proceeding, and a minor victim's parent or guardian may request them on the victim's behalf. Nothing in the section contemplates a petition, motion, application, request or filing of any kind by the person whose records close. Closure happens by operation of law on final termination, which for a suspended imposition of sentence means completion of probation. The review's enumeration of the statutory exceptions was left undone on its pass; there is exactly one, and it is a victim-access exception rather than a category of case that fails to close.
exclusions: Any case that has not been finally terminated. For a suspended imposition of sentence that means probation is still running; closure does not occur until it ends.
A conviction, a guilty plea followed by a suspended execution of sentence, or any disposition other than the four in § 610.105.1. Those close only through a § 610.140 petition, if at all.
The judgment or order of the court itself, which § 610.105.1 expressly keeps a public record even after the rest of the file closes.

Not an exception to closure but a limit on it: under § 610.105.2, where the charge was a chapter 566 offense or one of the enumerated offenses in §§ 568.045, 568.050, 568.060, 568.065, 568.175, 573.200 or 573.205 and imposition of sentence was suspended, the records are made available to the victim for use in the victim's own judicial proceeding.
The access § 610.120 preserves for law enforcement, courts, and the other entities that section names. Closure is not invisibility.

Where a case that should have closed is still public, the guidance stops and refers out. No determination that closure failed is ever made here, and no correction petition is invented for a remedy Missouri does not provide.

packetInstructions: Closure is not expungement and the guidance must keep them apart. A closed § 610.105 record leaves the judgment or order a public record, preserves the access § 610.120 grants, and may be reached by a victim under § 610.105.2. A § 610.140 order does more. Telling a participant their case is closed is not telling them it is gone.

Only a fingerprint-based Highway Patrol search shows records that are already closed. A name-based search cannot confirm closure; it can only fail to show the record, which is not the same answer. The guidance must say so or the participant will draw the wrong conclusion from a clean name-based result.
participantQuestions: A suspended imposition of sentence and a suspended execution of sentence are asked apart before anything else. The first closes automatically on completion of probation; the second is a conviction and does not close at all. Participants conflate them constantly and the consequence of getting it wrong is a wasted filing or a missed remedy.

Whether the case still appears on Case.net, on the Highway Patrol record and on any third-party background check are asked separately, because the three are different systems with different remedies and a participant reporting the record is still out there usually means only one of them.
scopeRestrictions: The track covers only the four § 610.105.1 dispositions — nolle prosequi, dismissal, not guilty, and suspended imposition of sentence — plus the § 552.030 mental-disease acquittal. Anything else is routed elsewhere and no closure is asserted for it.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether closure under § 610.105 reaches arresting-agency records and central-repository entries, or only the records of the court in which the case originated. The section speaks of official records pertaining to the case becoming closed records, which is broad, and § 610.120 governs who may still see a closed record; but the section does not enumerate custodians and does not direct any agency to act. It determines what the participant should expect to see on a Highway Patrol record and on a background check, and the review left it open.

releaseBlockers.question: Whether Missouri provides any participant-facing mechanism to compel closure where § 610.105 closure did not take effect. None was located: the section creates no remedy, no Office of the State Courts Administrator form addresses it, and the Highway Patrol's record-review challenge procedure runs through the Patrol and back to the reporting agency rather than through a court. The track therefore retains pure guidance and refers the participant out rather than asserting a route. If counsel identifies a motion, application or written demand that does exist, this becomes a packet.

openLegalQuestions.question: Whether a participant whose case closed under § 610.105 obtains any material benefit from also petitioning under § 610.140. The two have different effects — closure leaves the judgment a public record and preserves § 610.120 access, while a § 610.140 order restores civil rights, is a complete removal of all effects for 18 U.S.C. § 921(a)(33)(B)(ii) purposes, and directs named entities to close their own records — but § 610.140 consumes a lifetime cap slot and costs a filing fee. The trade-off is real and the guidance presents it as a question rather than a recommendation.

openLegalQuestions.question: The review left the statutory exceptions to § 610.105 closure unenumerated on its pass. They are now enumerated from the current text and there is exactly one: § 610.105.2's victim-access provision for a suspended imposition of sentence on a chapter 566 offense or one of the enumerated offenses in §§ 568.045, 568.050, 568.060, 568.065, 568.175, 573.200 or 573.205. This closes the review's open item rather than leaving it, and is recorded so the closure is traceable.

selfHelpStopConditions: A case that appears to qualify is still showing publicly on Case.net or on the Highway Patrol record after final termination.
The participant cannot tell from the docket whether the disposition was a suspended imposition of sentence or a suspended execution of sentence.
The participant is unsure whether a suspended imposition of sentence reached final termination, or probation was revoked.
A background check run by an employer, landlord or licensing body shows a case the participant believes is closed.
The charge was a chapter 566 offense or one of the offenses listed in § 610.105.2 and the participant is concerned about victim access to the file.
The participant wants the record corrected at the Highway Patrol or at the arresting agency rather than merely confirmed.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence, where closure is not the same as expungement for federal purposes.
The participant wants to know whether a § 610.140 petition would add anything to a case already closed.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether closure under § 610.105 reaches arresting-agency records and central-repository entries, or only the records of the court in which the case originated. The section speaks of official records pertaining to the case becoming closed records, which is broad, and § 610.120 governs who may still see a closed record; but the section does not enumerate custodians and does not direct any agency to act. It determines what the participant should expect to see on a Highway Patrol record and on a background check, and the review left it open.

provenance.sourceStatement: Whether closure under § 610.105 reaches arresting-agency records or only court records. Unresolved and it determines what the participant should expect.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether Missouri provides any participant-facing mechanism to compel closure where § 610.105 closure did not take effect. None was located: the section creates no remedy, no Office of the State Courts Administrator form addresses it, and the Highway Patrol's record-review challenge procedure runs through the Patrol and back to the reporting agency rather than through a court. The track therefore retains pure guidance and refers the participant out rather than asserting a route. If counsel identifies a motion, application or written demand that does exist, this becomes a packet.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether a participant whose case closed under § 610.105 obtains any material benefit from also petitioning under § 610.140. The two have different effects — closure leaves the judgment a public record and preserves § 610.120 access, while a § 610.140 order restores civil rights, is a complete removal of all effects for 18 U.S.C. § 921(a)(33)(B)(ii) purposes, and directs named entities to close their own records — but § 610.140 consumes a lifetime cap slot and costs a filing fee. The trade-off is real and the guidance presents it as a question rather than a recommendation.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Closure is not expungement and the guidance must keep them apart. A closed § 610.105 record leaves the judgment or order a public record, preserves the access § 610.120 grants, and may be reached by a victim under § 610.105.2. A § 610.140 order does more. Telling a participant their case is closed is not telling them it is gone.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 3 - Automatic closure of terminated cases
provenance.sourceStatement: If closure occurred, advise that no filing is needed and explain the difference between closure and expungement.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Only a fingerprint-based Highway Patrol search shows records that are already closed. A name-based search cannot confirm closure; it can only fail to show the record, which is not the same answer. The guidance must say so or the participant will draw the wrong conclusion from a clean name-based result.

provenance.sourceStatement: Use fingerprint-based where the participant needs to see closed records, since that is the only way to see what is already closed under § 610.105.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: A suspended imposition of sentence and a suspended execution of sentence are asked apart before anything else. The first closes automatically on completion of probation; the second is a conviction and does not close at all. Participants conflate them constantly and the consequence of getting it wrong is a wasted filing or a missed remedy.

tracks.legalName: Verified Petition for Expungement of Arrest Records (Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 610.122, 610.123 and 610.124)
tracks.publicName: An arrest based on false information
tracks.mechanism: Sections 610.122, 610.123 and 610.124 were read in full from the Revisor's current text and together they are the strongest record-clearing remedy Missouri has. § 610.122, effective 28 August 2021, allows any record of arrest recorded under § 43.503 to be expunged on either of two alternative grounds. The first is that the court determines the arrest was based on false information and that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge to believe the individual committed the offense, no charges will be pursued as a result of the arrest, and the subject did not receive a suspended imposition of sentence for the offense of arrest or any related offense. The second is that the court determines the person was arrested for, or subsequently charged with, a misdemeanor offense of chapter 303 or any moving violation as defined in § 302.010 other than an intoxication-related traffic offense as defined in § 577.023, that each offense or violation related to the arrest was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, and that the person is not a commercial driver's licence holder and was not operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the arrest. § 610.122.2 adds that a record is eligible only if no civil action is pending relating to the arrest or the records sought to be expunged. § 610.123 supplies the procedure and it is unusually specific: a verified petition filed in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest, which shall be dismissed if it does not contain the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, Social Security number and address at the time of arrest, the offense charged, the date of arrest, the county and any municipality of arrest, the arresting agency, the case number and court, and the petitioner's fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card at the time of filing, forwarded to the central repository for the sole purpose of positively identifying the petitioner. The petition names as defendants all law enforcement agencies, courts, prosecuting attorneys, central state depositories and others the petitioner has reason to believe may possess the records, and the court's order does not affect any person or entity not named. The court sets a hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing and gives reasonable notice to each named entity. § 610.123.4 makes relief mandatory on the findings — if the court finds the petitioner is entitled to expungement of any record that is the subject of the petition, it shall enter an order directing expungement — which closes an open question the review could not answer. § 610.124 then requires that all records ordered expunged be destroyed, or blacked out where destruction is not feasible because of the permanent nature of the record books, removed from all electronic files maintained with the State of Missouri, and that the central repository request the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge the records from its files. § 610.124.2 gives any petitioner, or agency protesting the expungement, the ordinary civil right of appeal. This is the one Missouri track where the word destroyed is accurate.
exclusions: Any arrest where the subject received a suspended imposition of sentence for the offense of arrest or for any offense related to the arrest (§ 610.122.1(1)(c)). This bars the false-information ground outright.

Any record where a civil action is pending relating to the arrest or to the records sought to be expunged (§ 610.122.2). This is a bar on both grounds and it reaches civil actions the participant may not think of as related.

On the moving-violation ground, any intoxication-related traffic offense or intoxication-related boating offense as defined under § 577.001. Those are excluded expressly and belong on the § 610.130 route if anywhere.
On the moving-violation ground, any person who is a commercial driver's licence holder or who was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the arrest (§ 610.122.1(2)(b)).
On the moving-violation ground, any offense or violation related to the arrest that was not nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted. Every related offense must have ended that way.
An offense that is neither a chapter 303 misdemeanor nor a moving violation as defined in § 302.010, where the participant is relying on the moving-violation ground rather than on false information.
An arrest that resulted in a conviction, which is not reachable under § 610.122 on either ground and runs on § 610.140 instead.

waitingPeriods.condition: Both grounds (§§ 610.122 and 610.123)
waitingPeriods.duration: none. Neither § 610.122 nor § 610.123 states a waiting period, and none is implied. What the false-information ground requires instead is a present-tense finding — that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge — so the question is the state of the evidence now rather than the passage of time.

tracks.venue: The civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest (§ 610.123.1). Both the court and the division differ from the § 610.140 routes: this is a civil action, not a criminal-side petition, and it is fixed to the arrest county rather than to the court of charge. Where the arrest occurred in a municipality the municipality is named in the petition but the filing is still in the circuit court's civil division for that county.

destination.name: Civil division of the Missouri circuit court in the county of arrest
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the circuit court, civil division, for the county where the arrest occurred. The clerk then does three things the printed instructions on CR145 set out: issues a copy of the petition to the prosecuting attorney; sends a copy of the petition and the fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository at the Highway Patrol; and gives notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney and to each official, agency or other entity named in the petition. The court sets the hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing.

components.conditionDescription: Generated where the participant's circuit expects the petitioner to tender a proposed judgment rather than the court preparing it.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: A local law enforcement agency — a municipal police department or county sheriff's department that takes applicant prints

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have you arranged to get three standard fingerprint cards from a local law enforcement agency? You need them before you file." against Three standard fingerprint cards, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Arrest report or booking record. Make an open-records request to the arresting agency for the arrest or booking record. It supplies the date of arrest, the citation number, the offense charged and the agency name, all of which § 610.123 makes mandatory contents of the petition.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The arresting law enforcement agency

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "On what date were you arrested?" against Arrest report or booking record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Certified record of the dismissal, nolle prosequi or not-guilty finding. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the entry disposing of each offense related to the arrest. The ground requires that every related offense or violation was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, so the participant needs the disposition for each one, not just the lead charge.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the charge was filed
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where a charge was filed and the participant is relying on the chapter 303 or moving-violation ground.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where a charge was filed and the participant is relying on the chapter 303 or moving-violation ground.
