packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.

One complete form set per conviction, never a consolidated petition. The OCA instructions require a separate form for each conviction even where the convictions occurred at the same time. This is the opposite of the misdemeanour expungement track, where one petition covers the whole record, and the rules engine must not generalise across the two.

Fee lookup must branch on court level and must not default to the District Court figure. The $120 civil commencement fee is the District Court schedule; Justice, Municipal and City Court fees are different and were not resolved. The OCA instructions confirm the participant is responsible for filing fees and other costs.

The OCA instructions state expressly that the participant must follow all applicable filing rules including local filing rules, and route the participant to the Court Locator for local rules and contact information. This is an acknowledged local-practice dependency and is built as a required lookup step.

§ 16-12-113(12) is express: petitioning under that section does not make a person ineligible to petition for misdemeanour expungement under Title 46, chapter 18, part 11. A participant can use both, and the eligibility engine must present them as complementary rather than alternative.
Note that § 16-12-113(5)(b) keys service to the county in which the petition is filed, not the county of prosecution.
participantQuestions: LegalEase does not choose among expungement, redesignation as a misdemeanour, and redesignation as a civil infraction. These are materially different outcomes with different consequences, the form requires the participant to choose, and the election is the participant's alone. Any analysis of which outcome is better is legal advice and triggers handoff.
scopeRestrictions: The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

No participant-facing statement that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, after a deferred dismissal, or after a non-conviction removal. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in any of the three statutes, and whether a cleared record may lawfully be denied is a hard self-help stop.

releaseBlockers.question: Which CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form version the Department of Justice enforces in practice, and what the current required attachment set is. The 2023 PDF and the 29 April 2024 DOCX disagree: the 2023 version requires valid photo identification for the Non-Conviction Removal and Deferred Imposition request types and requires the 'Original Court Order' for misdemeanour expungement, while the 2024 version drops the photo-ID requirement, requires the 'Original Court Judgement' instead, and adds 'Deferred Prosecution' to the fourth request type. Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the 2024 version as the supporting-process asset and does not retain the 2023 PDF. The 2024 version is used for legal design and the 2023 version is preserved as history only; the packet includes photo identification by default, which is the fail-closed reading, and asks for a certified copy of the judgment.

provenance.sourceStatement: The 2023 and 2024 CRISS form versions disagree on required attachments. The 2023 PDF requires valid photo identification for the Non-Conviction Removal and Deferred Imposition request types and requires the "Original Court Order" for misdemeanor expungement. The 2024 DOCX drops the photo ID requirement, requires the "Original Court Judgement" instead, and adds "Deferred Prosecution" to the fourth request type. Unresolved which set CRISS enforces in practice.

releaseBlockers.question: Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form as a SUPPORTING_PROCESS asset with document role SUPPORTING_FORM, not as a packet form. The authority gate treats a supporting-process asset as one that cannot back an official_pdf_fill component, so every Montana component that maps to it is recorded as an authority role mismatch. The classification is the issue, not the mechanism: the form is a genuine Department of Justice agency form, it carries no use restriction, § 46-18-1110(2)(b) and § 46-18-204(2) both refer to a form prepared by the department of justice, and it is the required and only vehicle for the DOJ stage of four Montana tracks and for the whole of the non-conviction removal track. The mapping is retained rather than dropped, because pointing at the retained asset is truthful and preserves traceability, and the asset-class question is carried here as an explicit release blocker and a proposed Edition 1.2 reclassification. Edition 1.1 is not modified.

releaseBlockers.question: Master Library Edition 1.1 gives the OCA MMRTA Proposed Order and the OCA MMRTA Certificate of Service the SAME document ID, MT-OCA-MMRTA, distinguished only by document role, ORDER against SERVICE. They are two different binaries with two different SHA-256 values, so a component that names MT-OCA-MMRTA matches two retained assets carrying conflicting hashes and the authority gate records an authority hash conflict. This is an Edition 1.1 source-identity problem rather than a defect in the Montana legal design: both forms exist, both are published by the Office of the Court Administrator, both are retained, and both are correctly placed in the packet. Each needs its own document ID in a successor edition before either component can be resolver-selectable. The mappings are retained and the tracks stay authority-gated.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): The text of the Temporary Rules adopted by Montana Supreme Court order AF 22-0129, filed 15 March 2022. The order was retrieved; the attached rules were not. They govern procedure for both MMRTA tracks and may contain filing, service or hearing requirements not reflected on the OCA forms. Relatedly, whether the 21-day county attorney response window is stated in the Temporary Rules or is OCA guidance only — it is currently sourced to the OCA instructions.

Open question blocks release (packet_components): Which CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form version the Department of Justice enforces in practice, and what the current required attachment set is. The 2023 PDF and the 29 April 2024 DOCX disagree: the 2023 version requires valid photo identification for the Non-Conviction Removal and Deferred Imposition request types and requires the 'Original Court Order' for misdemeanour expungement, while the 2024 version drops the photo-ID requirement, requires the 'Original Court Judgement' instead, and adds 'Deferred Prosecution' to the fourth request type. Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the 2024 version as the supporting-process asset and does not retain the 2023 PDF. The 2024 version is used for legal design and the 2023 version is preserved as history only; the packet includes photo identification by default, which is the fail-closed reading, and asks for a certified copy of the judgment.

Open question blocks release (filing_process): Whether any Montana district, justice, municipal or city court imposes a local form, local cover sheet or local addendum for any of these routes. Both the OCA MMRTA instructions and the deferred-dismissal guidance expressly warn of local variation, and the OCA instructions direct the participant to the Court Locator for local rules. Unresolved and material: it is why every court-filing track carries a clerk-contact step and why the deferred track carries a local-form override.

Open question blocks release (packet_components): Whether the Montana Supreme Court has adopted a court-approved statewide fee-waiver form, or whether the MLSA Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees is the only published option. It determines whether LegalEase can ship a fee-waiver component at all. Until resolved the packet links the participant to the published form rather than reproducing it, because the MLSA form carries the same non-commercial restriction as ER-100, ER-200, DS-100 and DS-200.

Open question blocks release (legal_effect_or_warning): Whether an expunged Montana misdemeanour, a dismissed deferred imposition, or a removed non-conviction may lawfully be denied in response to a general inquiry. No Montana perjury shield or restoration provision was located in Title 46 chapter 18 part 11, § 46-18-204 or § 44-5-202. Until answered the packet says nothing about denial and treats the question as a hard self-help stop.

Open question blocks release (correct_form): Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form as a SUPPORTING_PROCESS asset with document role SUPPORTING_FORM, not as a packet form. The authority gate treats a supporting-process asset as one that cannot back an official_pdf_fill component, so every Montana component that maps to it is recorded as an authority role mismatch. The classification is the issue, not the mechanism: the form is a genuine Department of Justice agency form, it carries no use restriction, § 46-18-1110(2)(b) and § 46-18-204(2) both refer to a form prepared by the department of justice, and it is the required and only vehicle for the DOJ stage of four Montana tracks and for the whole of the non-conviction removal track. The mapping is retained rather than dropped, because pointing at the retained asset is truthful and preserves traceability, and the asset-class question is carried here as an explicit release blocker and a proposed Edition 1.2 reclassification. Edition 1.1 is not modified.

Open question blocks release (correct_form): Master Library Edition 1.1 gives the OCA MMRTA Proposed Order and the OCA MMRTA Certificate of Service the SAME document ID, MT-OCA-MMRTA, distinguished only by document role, ORDER against SERVICE. They are two different binaries with two different SHA-256 values, so a component that names MT-OCA-MMRTA matches two retained assets carrying conflicting hashes and the authority gate records an authority hash conflict. This is an Edition 1.1 source-identity problem rather than a defect in the Montana legal design: both forms exist, both are published by the Office of the Court Administrator, both are retained, and both are correctly placed in the packet. Each needs its own document ID in a successor edition before either component can be resolver-selectable. The mappings are retained and the tracks stay authority-gated.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement or Resentencing of a Marijuana Conviction While Currently Serving (Mont. Code Ann. § 16-12-113(1)-(4), (8)-(12))
tracks.publicName: Marijuana conviction expungement or resentencing while serving a sentence
tracks.mechanism: Under § 16-12-113(1) a person CURRENTLY SERVING a sentence for an act that is permitted under Title 16, chapter 12, or that is punishable by a lesser sentence under that chapter than the person was awarded, may petition for expungement or resentencing. Section 16-12-113(2) directs the court to presume the petitioner satisfies the criteria unless the county attorney provides a reasonable basis otherwise, and, where the criteria are satisfied, to grant the petition UNLESS the court determines that granting it would pose an unreasonable risk of danger to public safety. That public-safety override does not appear in the subsection (6) pathway used by the completed-sentence track, and it is the principal reason the two are separate mechanisms rather than branches. Section 16-12-113(3) requires credit for time already served and prohibits supervision after resentencing; § 16-12-113(4) prohibits a term longer than the original sentence and prohibits reinstatement of charges dismissed under a negotiated plea agreement. Sections 16-12-114 through 16-12-116 define an expungement or resentencing of marijuana conviction court and authorise appointment of a decriminalized marijuana conviction expungement judge with the authority and power of an elected district court judge. Procedure is governed by the AF 22-0129 Temporary Rules and the Office of the Court Administrator publishes Form A specifically for the currently-serving posture, with the same Certificate of Service and Proposed Order.
exclusions: Acts that remain criminal at the same level under Title 16, chapter 12.
Non-marijuana controlled substance convictions.
Convictions from out-of-state, federal or Tribal courts.
A participant who has completed the sentence, who belongs on the completed-sentence track under § 16-12-113(5).
Relief may still be refused where the court determines that granting the petition would pose an unreasonable risk of danger to public safety (§ 16-12-113(2)). That override is unique to this track.

units.label: MMRTA Form A petition in the sentencing court, with certificate of service and proposed order
units.description: The court stage, and the substantive heart of the track. MMRTA Form A is published by the Office of the Court Administrator specifically for the currently-serving posture: the caption, the 'I am currently serving my sentence for this conviction' recital and the resentencing election are all built into it. The adopted Batch 2 resolution memorandum controls here and is explicit that Form A is a packet product and that the currently-serving posture is a scope restriction and a substantive-choice warning rather than a reason to downgrade the mechanism to guidance. LegalEase completes the caption for the correct court level, the participant's identity and case facts, the offence selection the participant makes from the enumerated list, and the conviction date, and assembles the OCA Certificate of Service and the OCA Proposed Order. It does not choose between expungement and resentencing, does not calculate a resentencing result, and does not author any public-safety argument. Required attachments are the participant's DOJ criminal record and the supporting court documents.

units.label: Conditional DOJ CRISS submission, only where the court grants expungement
units.description: The conditional Department of Justice stage. Where the court grants EXPUNGEMENT the participant must separately submit the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form with the court judgment and the expungement order, because the court order does not itself clear the DOJ criminal history record. Where the outcome is RESENTENCING rather than expungement the conviction stands with a modified sentence, there is nothing for DOJ to delete, and this unit does not apply — the packet says so plainly rather than sending a request that will be refused. That conditionality is why the unit exists as a distinct unit rather than as a step inside unit 1.

tracks.venue: Whichever court sentenced the participant, on the same three caption options as the completed-sentence track. The offence-mapping question is a self-help boundary: whether the historical conduct is now permitted, or is now punishable by a lesser sentence, under Title 16, chapter 12 requires mapping decades-old charging language and quantities against the current chapter, and it is the central legal question of the track. LegalEase presents the enumerated statutory list and the participant selects; the free-text specify-offence path is an attorney handoff.

packetInstructions: YES — STAGED OFFICIAL-FORM PACKET. OCA MMRTA Form A is expressly designed for the currently-serving posture. That posture is a scope restriction and a substantive-choice warning, not a reason to downgrade the mechanism to guidance. LegalEase must not choose between expungement, misdemeanor resentencing, and civil-infraction resentencing or author a public-safety argument. After an expungement outcome, the participant must complete the separate DOJ CRISS stage.

Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

One complete form set per conviction, never a consolidated petition. The OCA instructions require a separate form for each conviction even where the convictions occurred at the same time. This is the opposite of the misdemeanour expungement track, where one petition covers the whole record, and the rules engine must not generalise across the two.

The OCA instructions state expressly that the participant must follow all applicable filing rules including local filing rules, and route the participant to the Court Locator for local rules and contact information. This is an acknowledged local-practice dependency and is built as a required lookup step.
participantQuestions: LegalEase does not choose among expungement, redesignation as a misdemeanour, and redesignation as a civil infraction. These are materially different outcomes with different consequences, the form requires the participant to choose, and the election is the participant's alone. Any analysis of which outcome is better is legal advice and triggers handoff.
scopeRestrictions: Approve ordinary route; current-sentence posture is a scope restriction; obtain companion OCA forms.
The public-safety override in § 16-12-113(2) is unique to this track and does not appear in the completed-sentence pathway. Any case where it is plausibly in play is a handoff.

The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

legalDesignLimitations.statement: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

provenance.sourceStatement: Correct jurisdiction-specific terminology: "Expungement." Montana defines the word narrowly at § 46-18-1103(1): to permanently destroy, delete, or erase a record of an offense from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law enforcement agencies, and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Do not use the two words interchangeably in participant copy.

This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. legalDesignLimitations.statement: The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

tracks.legalName: Motion to Strike Plea or Verdict, Dismiss Charge, and Seal Case After a Completed Deferred Imposition (Mont. Code Ann. § 46-18-204)
tracks.publicName: Dismissal and sealing after a completed deferred sentence
tracks.mechanism: Section 46-18-204 has two limbs sharing one process, one destination, one document set and one legal effect, differing only on whether relief is mandatory. Under § 46-18-204(1)(a), on a FELONY deferred imposition, after termination of the deferral period or upon termination of the time remaining under § 46-18-208, the court SHALL strike the plea of guilty or nolo contendere or the verdict of guilty and order the charge dismissed, PROVIDED THAT a petition for revocation under § 46-18-203 has not been filed. Under § 46-18-204(1)(b), on a MISDEMEANOUR deferred imposition, upon motion of the court, the defendant or the defendant's attorney, the court MAY allow withdrawal of the plea or strike the verdict and order dismissal — discretionary, with no statutory factors. After dismissal, all records and data relating to the charge are confidential criminal justice information as defined in § 44-5-103, and public access may be obtained only by district court order upon good cause shown. This is sealing, not expungement: the record is not destroyed, and per DOJ the agencies listed in § 44-5-103 retain access to the sealed record in its entirety, DOJ specifically naming law enforcement including the military and Border Patrol. Section 46-18-204(2) puts the second stage on the participant: a copy of the order of dismissal must be sent to the prosecutor and to the Department of Justice with the DOJ form. Amended by Sec. 25, Ch. 321, L. 2017; no amendment since.
exclusions: A felony case in which a petition for revocation under § 46-18-203 was filed. That is the operative bar on the mandatory limb and it defeats § 46-18-204(1)(a) outright.

A SUSPENDED sentence. The published guidance states expressly that it does not apply to suspended sentences, and a participant who received a suspended rather than a deferred sentence is outside this route entirely.
A participant seeking early termination under § 46-18-208 rather than post-completion dismissal.
A deferral period that has not terminated and where no early termination under § 46-18-208 has occurred.
A case the court has already dismissed and sealed on its own, which the published guidance warns may have happened. The clerk-contact step is designed to catch this before anything is filed.

waitingPeriods.condition: Felony or misdemeanour deferred imposition
waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond expiry of the deferral period, or termination of the time remaining under § 46-18-208. There is no additional waiting period and, unlike the misdemeanour expungement track, this is not once in a lifetime.

units.label: Motion in the sentencing court to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge and seal the case
units.description: The court stage. A motion to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge and seal the case, with a certificate of service and a proposed order, filed in the court that issued the deferred sentence, under the SAME case number as the original criminal case. This is a motion in the existing criminal case rather than a new civil action, which is why no new filing fee is ordinarily expected. Section 46-18-204 prescribes no form, and the only published forms — DS-100 and DS-200 — carry the same non-commercial-use restriction as the misdemeanour expungement packet and cannot be shipped in a paid packet, so LegalEase drafts its own. The motion pleads the crime of conviction and whether it is a misdemeanour or a felony; whether the defendant pleaded guilty or nolo contendere or was found guilty by verdict; the date of sentencing and the fact of a deferred sentence; that the period of deferral has expired; that the defendant complied with all conditions; and that the prosecuting agency did not file a petition to revoke during the deferral period. The felony limb recites the mandatory shall and the no-revocation-petition proviso expressly; the misdemeanour limb is pleaded as discretionary. The prayer asks the court to strike the plea or verdict, dismiss the charge, seal the case, classify all records and data as confidential criminal justice information accessible to the public only by district court order upon good cause shown, and send a copy of the order to the prosecuting agency, and recites that the defendant will be responsible for providing a copy to the Department of Justice. localFormOverride is set because the published guidance acknowledges that individual courts may have their own procedures or different forms, and a court's current local form takes precedence over the drafted motion.

units.label: DOJ CRISS submission after the dismissal order
units.description: The Department of Justice stage, a separate participant submission to a different destination that § 46-18-204(2) places on the participant. LegalEase completes the participant-owned fields of the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form with the deferred-imposition request type selected, and supplies the mailing checklist and the verification steps; the participant encloses the deferred sentence order and the dismissal order and mails them to CRISS. Without this stage the DOJ criminal history record continues to show the charge.

tracks.venue: The court that issued the deferred sentence — District, Justice, or Municipal or City Court — under the same case number as the original criminal case.

destination.name: The sentencing court, then the Department of Justice
destination.detail: Unit 1 is filed with the clerk of the sentencing court in the existing criminal case. Unit 2 is mailed to Montana Department of Justice, Division of Criminal Investigation, CRISS Expungement, 2225 11th Ave., P.O. Box 201403, Helena, MT 59620. Phone (406) 444-3625. Email dojcriss@mt.gov.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the deferred sentence order. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a copy of the deferred sentence order. It gives you the case number and the deferral period, and you will need it again at the DOJ stage.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Was your sentence DEFERRED, rather than suspended? These are different and this route only works for a deferred imposition. Your sentencing order should say which." against Copy of the deferred sentence order, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Confirmation from the court record that no petition to revoke was filed. Ask the clerk to confirm from the case file whether a petition to revoke was ever filed during the deferral period. On a felony this is dispositive: § 46-18-204(1)(a) makes dismissal mandatory only where no revocation petition was filed. LegalEase will not assert this for you.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Did the prosecuting agency ever file a petition to revoke your deferred sentence? If you are not sure, the clerk of court can tell you, and on a felony this is the fact that decides whether the court must grant your motion." against Confirmation from the court record that no petition to revoke was filed, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Obtain Copy of the dismissal order once granted. After the court signs the order, ask the clerk for a copy. It is enclosed with the CRISS request together with the deferred sentence order.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.

A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.

Stage 1, the call to the clerk, is a required packet step with a script. The published guidance says courts may have their own procedures or forms and that the case may already have been dismissed and sealed.
LegalEase drafts its own motion, certificate of service, and proposed order. It must not reproduce DS-100 or DS-200.

Participant-facing copy must say "sealed and treated as confidential criminal justice information," never "destroyed" or "erased." Agencies listed in § 44-5-103 retain access to the sealed record in its entirety, and DOJ specifically names law enforcement including the military and Border Patrol.
participantQuestions: Whether a petition to revoke was ever filed is dispositive for the felony limb and must be confirmed with the clerk rather than asserted from the participant's recollection.
scopeRestrictions: The Misdemeanor Expungement in Montana packet (ER-100, ER-200 and the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees) and the Dismissal After Completing a Deferred Sentence packet (DS-100 and DS-200) are stamped '© 2025 Montana Legal Services Association and Montana Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission. This form may be used for non-commercial purposes only.' Expungement.ai is a paid product, so reproducing or distributing them inside a packet is a commercial use. They are drafting references only: never generated, never relabelled, never converted, never lightly rewritten, never runtime-selectable and never generation_allowed. The restriction changes source use, not the existence of the mechanism.

No participant-facing statement that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, after a deferred dismissal, or after a non-conviction removal. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in any of the three statutes, and whether a cleared record may lawfully be denied is a hard self-help stop.
Immigration warning before generation. A dismissal after deferred imposition may still be a conviction for federal immigration purposes, and a noncitizen participant is a hard stop.

The qualifying felony deferred-imposition limb is mandatory where no revocation petition was filed; the misdemeanour limb remains discretionary with no statutory factors. The distinction must be preserved in the pleading and in participant expectations.
Local court procedures and forms remain release gates. localFormOverride is set and a court's current local form takes precedence over the drafted motion.

releaseBlockers.question: Which CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form version the Department of Justice enforces in practice, and what the current required attachment set is. The 2023 PDF and the 29 April 2024 DOCX disagree: the 2023 version requires valid photo identification for the Non-Conviction Removal and Deferred Imposition request types and requires the 'Original Court Order' for misdemeanour expungement, while the 2024 version drops the photo-ID requirement, requires the 'Original Court Judgement' instead, and adds 'Deferred Prosecution' to the fourth request type. Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the 2024 version as the supporting-process asset and does not retain the 2023 PDF. The 2024 version is used for legal design and the 2023 version is preserved as history only; the packet includes photo identification by default, which is the fail-closed reading, and asks for a certified copy of the judgment.

provenance.sourceStatement: The 2023 and 2024 CRISS form versions disagree on required attachments. Unresolved which set CRISS enforces in practice.

The authority gate treats a supporting-process asset as one that cannot back an official_pdf_fill component, so every Montana component that maps to it is recorded as an authority role mismatch. The classification is the issue, not the mechanism: the form is a genuine Department of Justice agency form, it carries no use restriction, § 46-18-1110(2)(b) and § 46-18-204(2) both refer to a form prepared by the department of justice, and it is the required and only vehicle for the DOJ stage of four Montana tracks and for the whole of the non-conviction removal track. Edition 1.1 is not modified.

tracks.legalName: Non-Conviction Record Removal Request to DOJ CRISS (Mont. Code Ann. § 44-5-202(8))
tracks.publicName: Non-conviction record removal
tracks.mechanism: Montana distinguishes removal, where the record is deleted from the database and hard copy destroyed, from sealing under § 46-18-204, where the record persists but is confidential. Section 44-5-202(8), read with § 44-5-213(2), compels the disposition to be reported to the state repository within fourteen business days, requires photographs and fingerprints to be returned to the originating agency which shall expunge all copies, and provides that a criminal justice agency may not maintain any copies. DOJ publishes a single agency form, the Expungement/Removal Request Form, with a dedicated Non-Conviction Removal request type, and its published list of eligible dispositions is charges dismissed, deferred prosecution dismissed, acquitted, charges dropped and charges not filed; in statute the categories are released without the filing of charges, charges that did not result in a conviction, and a conviction later invalidated. Two gaps must be recorded rather than papered over. First, § 44-5-202 is titled Photographs and fingerprints and subsection (8) by its terms compels expungement of PHOTOGRAPHS AND FINGERPRINTS; it does not on its face compel deletion of the criminal history record entry itself, and § 44-5-212 separately limits expunging, purging or destroying criminal justice information. DOJ nonetheless treats § 44-5-202(8) as the authority for removing non-conviction arrest data and instructs participants to quote it, so LegalEase follows the published practice but does not represent the outcome as legally guaranteed beyond the photographs and fingerprints. Second, § 44-5-202(8) reaches the state repository and originating agencies and does NOT reach court records; Montana has no comparable authority to seal non-conviction court records and no centralised court records system, so a participant who succeeds here may still find the case on a county court portal.

A deferred imposition that has not yet been dismissed. DOJ routes those back to the court, which means the deferred-dismissal track comes first.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.
Participant-facing copy must state clearly that this track does not reach court records and that the case may still appear on a county court portal.
Do not describe the outcome as legally guaranteed beyond photographs and fingerprints; the cited statute is narrower than the published DOJ practice.
The CHOPRS check is a required prerequisite step, per DOJ, and must be run before the request is submitted.
Include photo ID by default pending resolution of the 2023 versus 2024 form discrepancy.
scopeRestrictions: No participant-facing statement that the participant may deny the conviction after expungement, after a deferred dismissal, or after a non-conviction removal. No Montana perjury shield or restoration-to-prior-status provision was located in any of the three statutes, and whether a cleared record may lawfully be denied is a hard self-help stop.
A deferred imposition not yet dismissed routes to the deferred-dismissal track first, and a revoked deferred sentence is treated by DOJ as a conviction and is outside this route.

The classification is the issue, not the mechanism: the form is a genuine Department of Justice agency form, it carries no use restriction, § 46-18-1110(2)(b) and § 46-18-204(2) both refer to a form prepared by the department of justice, and it is the required and only vehicle for the DOJ stage of four Montana tracks and for the whole of the non-conviction removal track. tracks.legalName: Automatic Non-Conviction Removal for Post-July-2017 Dispositions (Mont. Code Ann. § 44-5-202(8))
tracks.publicName: Automatic non-conviction removal
tracks.mechanism: Section 44-5-202(8), as amended by Ch. 321, L. 2017 effective 1 July 2017 and read with § 44-5-213(2), underpins a DOJ practice of removing non-conviction arrest data without any participant request. The Montana Department of Justice states on its Non-Conviction Removal and Sealing page that after 1 July 2017 CRISS will automatically remove all non-conviction arrest data per § 44-5-202 and that NO Record Removal Form is required. The trigger is the court's report of the disposition to the state repository, which the statute requires within fourteen business days. Relief is mandatory and automatic, there is no waiting period and no case-count limit, and there is no petition, application, motion or form for a participant to submit. The only practical question on this route is whether a record that has not been removed is ineligible or is simply the product of a court that failed to report the disposition, which is a records problem rather than a legal one.
exclusions: Dispositions occurring before 1 July 2017, which are not reached by the automatic practice and go to the non-conviction removal request route instead.
Convictions.
A revoked deferred sentence, which the DOJ flowchart treats as a conviction.
Court records, which the automatic removal does not reach and which remain publicly searchable on the county court portal.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Non-Conviction Records Pursuant to Pa.R.Crim.P. 790
tracks.publicName: Expunge a Pennsylvania court case that did not end in a conviction
tracks.mechanism: Section 9122(a) requires expungement of criminal history record information where no disposition has been received or recorded within 18 months after the date of arrest and the court finds the conditions met, or where a court order requires nonconviction data to be expunged. Rule 790 prescribes the petition contents, the attached Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report, service on the attorney for the Commonwealth, and the expungement order for court cases.
exclusions: Mixed cases in which any charge in the case resulted in a conviction. Section 9122(a) reaches nonconviction data; a case with a conviction on any count is not a clean non-conviction.
Cases in which only summary offenses were filed and the case remained at the magisterial district court, which proceed under Pa.R.Crim.P. 490 instead.
Records held by federal, military, tribal or out-of-state authorities, which Pennsylvania relief does not reach.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Expungement Following Complete Acquittal
tracks.publicName: Check that a full acquittal cleared your record automatically
tracks.mechanism: Where a person is acquitted of all charges based on the same conduct or arising from the same criminal episode, § 9122(a) provides for expungement without a petition. The Commonwealth has 60 days to object and, where the statutory requirements are met, expungement occurs no later than 12 months from the date of acquittal.
exclusions: Partial acquittals. A person acquitted on some counts and convicted or otherwise disposed on others is outside this route entirely and is screened under the Rule 790 non-conviction track or the petition-based limited access track.
Cases where the acquitted and non-acquitted charges arose from different conduct or different criminal episodes.

exclusions: Any arrest or prosecution during the five-year period, even where it did not result in a conviction. The § 9122(b) standard is free of arrest or prosecution, which is stricter than the conviction-free standards used by limited access and Clean Slate.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of the Arrest Record on Successful Completion of Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition
tracks.publicName: Check that finishing ARD cleared your arrest record
tracks.mechanism: When the judge orders dismissal of the charges after successful completion of Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition, Rule 320 provides that the judge also shall order expungement of the defendant's arrest record, subject to a Commonwealth objection filed within 30 days after service of the motion for dismissal, on which the Commonwealth must show compelling reasons to retain the record. Section 9122(b.1) removes the court's authority to expunge the arrest record where ARD was granted for enumerated sexual offences and the victim was under 18.

tracks.legalName: Expungement Following an Unconditional Pardon
tracks.publicName: Clear a record after you receive a pardon
tracks.mechanism: A pardon is executive clemency and does not by itself erase the record. Where an unconditional pardon has been granted, § 9122 provides for expungement: the Board of Pardons transmits eligible records to the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts quarterly, the AOPC sends the record to the court of common pleas, and the court orders expungement after confirming the criteria. A conditional pardon may instead trigger Clean Slate limited access under § 9122.2(a)(4).
exclusions: Records for which no pardon has been granted. The pardon application itself is out of scope.
Conditional pardons, which are routed to Clean Slate limited access under § 9122.2(a)(4) rather than to expungement.

tracks.publicName: Petition to seal a Pennsylvania conviction from public view
tracks.mechanism: Section 9122.1(a) permits a petition for limited access to a qualifying misdemeanour or ungraded offence carrying a maximum penalty of no more than five years where the person has been free from conviction for a period of seven years, has completed all court-ordered restitution, and has paid the authorized fee. Section 9122.1(a.1), added by Act 36 of 2023, extends the petition to qualifying felonies other than felonies of the first and second degree where the person has been free from conviction for a period of ten years on the same conditions. Rule 791 prescribes the petition, the attached Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing, service on the attorney for the Commonwealth, and the order.
exclusions: Offences punishable by more than two years in the following categories, per § 9122.1(b): offences involving danger to the person under Article B of Part II; offences against the family under Article D; firearms and other dangerous articles under Chapter 61; offences requiring registration under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9799.14 or § 9799.55; and corruption of minors.

Prior-record bars under § 9122.1(b)(2): a conviction for murder or a felony of the first degree; certain serious offences within the preceding 15 years; and two or more offences punishable by more than two years within the preceding 10 years.
Felonies of the first and second degree, which are outside the § 9122.1(a.1) qualifying-felony route.
A drug felony on which a minimum sentence of 30 months or more, or a maximum sentence of 60 months or more, was imposed, which falls outside the § 9102 definition of qualifying offence.

tracks.legalName: Clean Slate Automatic Limited Access Under 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122.2
tracks.publicName: Check whether Clean Slate has sealed your record automatically
tracks.mechanism: Section 9122.2 provides automatic limited access without any petition. Subsection (a)(1) reaches a conviction of a misdemeanour of the second degree or a misdemeanour punishable by no more than two years where the person has been free for seven years from conviction for any offence punishable by imprisonment of one or more years. Subsection (a)(1.1) reaches a qualifying offence on the same terms after ten years. Subsection (a)(2) reaches charges resulting in a final disposition other than a conviction. Subsection (a)(3) reaches a summary conviction when five years have elapsed since entry of the judgment of conviction. Subsection (a)(4) reaches a conviction for which a conditional pardon was granted. Under subsection (b) the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts transmits eligible records to the Pennsylvania State Police central repository and removes records for which a notification of ineligibility is received.
exclusions: The exclusions in § 9122.3 are keyed by subsection rather than expressed as one generic ineligible-offence list. Section 9122.3(a) states that limited access under § 9122.2(a)(1) shall not be granted for the enumerated categories, and § 9122.3(a)(2) carries its own separate structure; § 9122.3(c) provides that an offence eligible for clean slate limited access is also eligible for a petition for limited access under § 9122.1. The subsection-specific structure is preserved and is not collapsed.
Offences requiring registration under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9799.14 or § 9799.55, and failure to comply with registration requirements under 18 Pa.C.S. § 4915.1, per § 9122.3(a)(1)(iv) and (a)(2)(iv)(C).
An otherwise qualifying conviction where a conviction punishable by five or more years, or another excluded offence, arose out of the same case, except for a qualifying offence.

tracks.legalName: Motion for Expungement of Arrest Record (SDCL §§ 23A-3-26 to 23A-3-32)
tracks.publicName: Expunge a South Dakota arrest record
tracks.mechanism: An arrested person may apply to the court that would have jurisdiction over the crime for which the person was arrested for an order expunging the record of the arrest: after one year from the arrest where no accusatory instrument was filed; after one year from the date the prosecuting attorney formally dismisses the entire criminal case on the record; at any time after an acquittal; or within one year of a formal dismissal of the entire case on a showing of compelling necessity. The motion starts a new civil action, may be made only on a record of arrest, and more than one arrest record requires a separate case for each. The court may enter the order only after finding by clear and convincing evidence that the ends of justice and the best interests of the public and the defendant or arrested person will be served. Expungement in South Dakota means sealing, not destruction, and a nonpublic disposition record is retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation.
exclusions: Partial dismissals. Both the statute and the review turn on the ENTIRE criminal case being formally dismissed on the record; where some counts were dismissed and others resolved otherwise, this track is unavailable.
Convictions of any kind, which this track does not reach; South Dakota is not a broad adult conviction-expungement state.
Federal, tribal, military and out-of-state records, which South Dakota relief does not reach.
More than one arrest record in a single filing; each arrest record requires its own civil action and its own fee.

units.label: Disposition classification, timing analysis and arrest-record count
units.description: The judgment stage, and the one that decides whether anything can be filed at all. Establish the correct court and county; establish whether the entire criminal case was formally dismissed on the record rather than partially; establish which of the four § 23A-3-27 timing branches applies and whether its clock has run; and count how many separate arrest records are involved, because each one requires its own civil action and its own $72 fee. The participant is directed to obtain the dismissal order, the acquittal judgment or proof that no accusatory instrument was filed, plus the court docket and a DCI criminal history. Nothing is filed at this stage and LegalEase does not receive, inspect or authenticate any of those records.

units.label: UJS motion packet: UJS-232, UJS-391 and the proposed UJS-394 order
units.description: The document stage. The South Dakota Unified Judicial System publishes a complete statewide form set, so the document work is form-fill and no custom pleading is advisable. LegalEase completes UJS-232 Case Filing Statement, UJS-391 Motion for Expungement and Statement of Mailing, and the proposed UJS-394 Order for Expungement which the judge signs. UJS-392 Waiver of Hearing is prepared conditionally, only where the arrested person, the prosecutor and any victim will all waive. UJS-393 Notice of Hearing is prepared conditionally where a hearing is required. The forms are identified by number and use but were not supplied in the archive; acquiring the current revisions is carried as a legal-design blocker on this track.

units.label: Filing, fee or indigency request, service on the State's Attorney, hearing or waiver, and UJS-395
units.description: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File the new civil action with the clerk and pay the $72 civil filing fee or request indigency relief; mail or serve the State's Attorney, who may contest; serve any notice of hearing at least fourteen days before the hearing; coordinate the three-party waiver where all of the person, the prosecutor and any victim agree; and after the order is signed prepare and file UJS-395 Notice of Entry of Order and mail it with the order to the State's Attorney. tracks.legalName: Expungement of Record on Completion of a Diversion Program (SDCL §§ 23A-3-35 to 23A-3-37)
tracks.publicName: Clear a record after completing a diversion program
tracks.mechanism: A person placed in a diversion program is eligible for expungement of the entire criminal record related to that arrest if they successfully completed all the terms of the program and have not been charged with any new crimes, except petty offences or minor traffic citations, within one year and thirty days from the date of successful completion. Where those requirements are met the State's Attorney shall file a dismissal of all charges related to the arrest and a notice of completion of the diversion program, and upon that filing the court shall grant the expungement without the filing of a motion or any further action by the court.
exclusions: Any new crime charged within one year and thirty days from successful completion, other than petty offences or minor traffic citations.
Incomplete diversion, or any term of the diversion programme not satisfied.
Anything short of the ENTIRE criminal record related to that arrest; the statute is framed around the entire record.
Federal, tribal, military and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Removal of Non-Felony Charges or Convictions from the Public Record (SDCL § 23A-3-34)
tracks.publicName: Automatic removal of a minor case from your public record
tracks.mechanism: Any charge or conviction resulting from a case where a petty offense, municipal ordinance violation or a Class 2 misdemeanor was the highest charged offense shall be automatically removed from a defendant's public record after five years if all court-ordered conditions on the case have been satisfied and the defendant has not been convicted of any further offenses within those five years. The case record remains available to court personnel or as authorized by order of the court and may be used as an enhancement in the prosecution of subsequent offenses as provided by law.
exclusions: Any case where the highest charged offense exceeded a Class 2 misdemeanor.
Any case with court-ordered conditions that have not been satisfied.
Any defendant convicted of a further offense within the five-year period.
Removal from the public record does not remove the record from court personnel, from access by order of the court, or from use as an enhancement in a later prosecution.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of Records on Discharge and Dismissal after a Suspended Imposition of Sentence (SDCL §§ 23A-27-13 to 23A-27-17)
tracks.publicName: Seal a record after a suspended imposition of sentence
tracks.mechanism: For certain offenses a court may suspend imposition of sentence where the person has never before been convicted of a felony. After the person completes all court conditions the defendant is discharged and the case is dismissed without adjudication of guilt, and the discharge and dismissal are not deemed a conviction for disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law. Upon the discharge and dismissal a court SHALL order that all official records, other than the nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation, be sealed along with all records relating to the arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, and dismissal and discharge. The order restores the person to the status occupied before arrest, indictment or information, and the person is not guilty of perjury or of giving a false statement for failing to recite or acknowledge the matter.
exclusions: Any person previously convicted of a felony, who is not eligible for a felony suspended imposition of sentence in the first place.
A second felony suspended imposition of sentence; the statute permits one felony SIS and one misdemeanor SIS per person.
Any case where the court conditions have not been completed and the discharge and dismissal have not issued.
The nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation, which are expressly excluded from the sealing order.
Federal, tribal, military and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of Records on the Grant of a Chapter 24-14 Pardon (SDCL § 24-14-11)
tracks.publicName: Records sealed after a governor's pardon
tracks.mechanism: A person granted a pardon under the provisions of chapter 24-14 is released from all disabilities consequent on the conviction. Upon the granting of such a pardon the Governor shall order that all official records relating to the pardoned person's arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, application for a pardon, and the proceedings of the Board of Pardons and Paroles be sealed. The Governor files a public document with the secretary of state certifying the pardon; that document remains public for five years and is then sealed. A pardon granted without following the provisions of the chapter may not be sealed. The pardon restores the person to their pre-arrest status and protects against perjury or false-statement liability for failing to acknowledge the matter, but the conviction may still be considered for sentencing on subsequent offences and habitual-offender determinations.
exclusions: Any pardon granted without following the provisions of chapter 24-14, which expressly may not be sealed.
The pardon application itself, which is a Board of Pardons and Paroles process requiring advocacy and is outside LegalEase self-help scope.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Arrest, Dismissal of Charges or Disposition (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1401)
tracks.publicName: Clear an arrest or dismissed charge
tracks.mechanism: On a verified petition to the court in which the proceeding occurred or would have occurred, the court may expunge records of an arrest, a charge that was dismissed, or a disposition where the person was not convicted, provided at least 180 days have passed, no formal charges are pending, and no disposition under § 7-13-301, § 35-7-1037 or former § 7-13-203 was entered to any charge arising from the incident, including to a different or lesser charge. Expungement classifies the record at the Division of Criminal Investigation so it is not disseminated except to criminal justice agencies for criminal justice purposes; the court file is sealed and a certified order is transmitted to DCI.
exclusions: Any disposition under Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-301, § 35-7-1037 or former § 7-13-203 entered to any charge resulting from the incident, including a disposition to a different or lesser charge.
Formal charges pending against the person at the time the petition is filed.

Records that are not maintained in the state central repository at the Division of Criminal Investigation, including investigatory files of any local, state or federal criminal justice agency used solely for criminal justice purposes.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

packetInstructions: Wyoming publishes no statewide expungement form. County clerks, municipal courts and circuit courts may have local templates or formatting requirements. Call the clerk of the court where the petition will be filed before finalizing, and use a local template where one exists. Never invent a statewide form number.

Adult expungement in Wyoming means classifying the record at DCI so it is not publicly disseminated. It does not destroy the record, criminal justice agencies retain access, and newspapers, private websites and private background-check databases are not reached. Nothing in Wyoming happens automatically, and DCI answers 'no' to whether adult arrests ever drop off a Wyoming record.
No order may issue before 20 days after service on the prosecuting attorney. Tell the participant that timing in the packet instructions rather than in the pleading.

Ask whether the participant was fingerprinted at arrest, because a Wyoming criminal history exists only where an arrest fingerprint card was submitted. A participant may have a court record with no DCI record, or the reverse, and that changes what expungement is worth to them.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Conviction of Certain Misdemeanors (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1501)
tracks.publicName: Clear a misdemeanor conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person who has pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or been convicted of, a misdemeanor may petition the convicting court to expunge the records of conviction. The waiting period is at least five years for non-status offenses and at least one year for status offenses as defined by § 7-1-107(b)(iii), measured from expiration of the terms of sentence including probation and any court-ordered program. The offense must not have involved the use or attempted use of a firearm; a health care provider convicted of a § 6-2-313 offense against a patient in their care is ineligible. The court must find the petitioner is not a substantial danger to himself, any identifiable victim or society. One expungement under this section is permitted in a lifetime. Per the Wyoming Judicial Branch, the section includes cases of deferred adjudication and cases where the charge was later dismissed.
exclusions: Misdemeanors involving the use or attempted use of a firearm.
A health care provider who pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or was convicted of, an offense punishable under Wyo. Stat. § 6-2-313 committed against a patient under that provider's care.
Any person who has previously received an expungement of records of conviction under § 7-13-1501; the statute permits one in a lifetime.
Felony convictions, which are handled under § 7-13-1502.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Conviction of Certain Felonies (Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1502)
tracks.publicName: Clear a felony conviction
tracks.mechanism: A person convicted of a felony, or of felonies subject to expungement under the section arising out of the same occurrence or related course of events, may petition the convicting court to expunge the records of conviction. At least ten years must have passed since expiration of the terms of sentence including probation; any court-ordered program must be complete and court-ordered restitution paid in full; the petitioner must have no other felony plea, nolo plea or conviction; the offense must not have involved the use or attempted use of a firearm except certain Title 23 offenses; and the offense must not appear on the statutory exclusion list. The court must find eligibility and that the petitioner is not a substantial danger to himself, any identifiable victim or society. One expungement under this section is permitted in a lifetime. Under subsection (m) the expungement restores any rights removed as a result of the conviction.
exclusions: Violent felonies under Wyo. Stat. § 6-1-104(a)(xii).
Aggravated homicide by vehicle; drug-induced homicide.
Sexual assault and related sexual offenses under Wyo. Stat. §§ 6-2-301 through 6-2-320.
Certain domestic battery offenses; child abuse; endangering children with controlled substances; incest; sexual exploitation of children.
Aggravated assault or battery on a corrections or detention officer; disarming a peace officer; escape from official detention and violent or armed escape.
Bribery.
Weapons offenses under Wyo. Stat. §§ 6-8-101 and 6-8-102.
Any offense subject to sex offender registration under Wyo. Stat. §§ 7-19-302(g) through (j).
Felonies involving the use or attempted use of a firearm, except certain Title 23 offenses.
Any petitioner who has previously pled guilty or nolo contendere to, or been convicted of, a felony other than the felony or felonies being expunged.
Any person who has previously received an expungement of records of conviction under § 7-13-1502; the statute permits one in a lifetime.
Federal, tribal and out-of-state records, which Wyoming relief does not reach.

rules.filing: File the verified Petition for Expungement of Records of Conviction and the proposed Order for Expungement with the clerk of the convicting court. Call that clerk about local templates and formatting before finalizing.
rules.fees: $300 filing fee per petition.
rules.feeWaiver: none
rules.notice: The prosecuting attorney has 90 days to object and no order may be granted before that window closes; the prosecutor, not the petitioner, notifies identifiable victims. The court must find both that the petitioner is eligible and that the petitioner does not represent a substantial danger to himself, any identifiable victim or society. If no objection is filed the court may summarily enter the order on finding eligibility.
rules.service: Serve the verified petition on the prosecuting attorney and on the Division of Criminal Investigation, and file proof of service.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and verifies the petition. Verification by the petitioner is required by statute.
rules.notarization: Verification is required by statute; confirm with the clerk of the convicting court whether that court requires the verification to be sworn before a notary.

Was there an identifiable victim in this case?
Are you now, or have you ever been, required to register as a sex offender for this offense?

selfHelpBoundaries: The felony may appear on the § 7-13-1502 exclusion list. The list is long and statute-specific and is not encoded; route to attorney review.
The participant has any other felony plea, nolo plea or conviction anywhere, since the other-felony bar looks at the entire record.
Any firearm use or attempted use, including where the participant believes a Title 23 carve-out applies.
Any offense subject to sex offender registration under §§ 7-19-302(g) through (j).
The participant has already received one expungement under § 7-13-1502; the statute allows one in a lifetime.
A completed felony deferral rather than a conviction. Section 7-13-1502 by its terms requires a conviction and § 7-13-1401 is barred by the deferral, so there may be no route at all. Stop and refer.
The prosecuting attorney files an objection, or the court sets a contested hearing.
An identifiable victim is likely to object.
Facts indicating human trafficking or coercion, which route to the § 6-2-708 vacatur outside this track.
Immigration consequences.
Federal, tribal or out-of-state records.
A completed felony deferral may have no Wyoming route at all. Stop and refer rather than guessing, and say so honestly.
packetInstructions: Tell the participant the felony track takes at least ninety days after service before an order can issue, making it a four-month engagement at minimum.

Tell the participant to obtain and attach proof that court-ordered restitution was paid in full, and that probation and any court-ordered program were completed. The ten-year clock runs from expiration of the terms of sentence.

Disclose before payment that § 7-13-1502 allows one felony expungement in a lifetime, and that DCI, its employees and prosecuting attorneys are immune from liability under § 7-13-1502(j) for actions, inactions or omissions under the section.
Recite the restoration-of-rights effect under § 7-13-1502(m) in the proposed order, and make no assertion about the effect of expungement on firearm rights beyond that statutory restoration language.
Wyoming publishes no statewide expungement form. Call the clerk of the convicting court about local templates and formatting before finalizing, and never invent a statewide form number.
participantQuestions: Ask whether the petitioner has any other felony plea, nolo plea or conviction anywhere. The other-felony bar looks at the entire record, and LegalEase must not assert that the petitioner has no other felony.
Ask whether the offense involved the use or attempted use of a firearm, including where a Title 23 carve-out may apply. LegalEase must not assert that no firearm was used.
scopeRestrictions: This track carries a mandatory attorney-review gate before the packet is offered, because the restoration-of-rights payoff makes it worth doing properly once.

releaseBlockers.question: Is the Lynch citation accurate? The proposition is consistent with the statutory text, which opens with 'a person convicted of a felony', but the citation could not be confirmed.
